papers.title: Swiss CPI microdata for research: data structure, panel construction, and applications
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper describes the microdata underlying the Swiss Consumer Price Index (CPI) and provides a fully reproducible pipeline for their use in empirical research. It documents the features most relevant for research—product hierarchy, collection methods, expenditure weights, temporary sales, product substitutions, and missing observations—and details a complete procedure for transforming the raw files into a research-ready price panel, making all design choices explicit. Two case studies illustrate how different research objectives map into different sample constructions: one reconstructing official CPI inflation, one tailored to the analysis of price-setting behavior. An open-source R repository implements every pipeline step, with key treatment choices available as configurable switches, allowing researchers with authorized data access to reproduce all results and adapt the pipeline to their own questions.
papers.reason: Offers methodological guidance and an open-source pipeline for researchers utilizing Swiss CPI microdata, with indirect market utility.

papers.title: Forecasting the price of carbon with macroeconomic and financial variables
papers.abstract: We tackle the issue of producing point, sign, and density forecasts for the monthly real price of carbon in the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). We show that Bayesian Vector Autoregressive (BVAR) models augmented with factors based on macroeconomic and financial variables yield improvements in point and density forecasting performance, with the largest point-forecast gains emerging at intermediate and longer horizons. In particular, the one-factor BVAR model provides lowest values at six and nine months ahead, while the baseline BVAR performs best at the one-year horizon. By contrast, a large BVAR including all predictors individually does not improve point forecast accuracy, supporting the use of parsimonious model specifications. Simple forecast pooling delivers modest gains from medium horizons onward, but does not mitigate the time variation in relative forecast performance. We also provide a qualitative comparison of model-based forecasts with survey expectations and forecasts released by data providers, which further highlights that relative forecast performance varies over time. Moreover, we consider verified emissions and show that stochastic volatility improves point forecasts, with reductions of about 6.5–7.1% at the one-year horizon. Lastly, we use model-based forecasts to construct market monitoring tools that track demand and price pressure in the EU ETS.
papers.reason: Evaluates forecasting models for EU ETS carbon prices using macroeconomic and financial variables, directly aiding carbon market monitoring and trading strategies.

papers.title: Reducing transport externalities through nudging: Results from a GPS-tracked experiment
papers.abstract: This study presents a randomized controlled trial in Switzerland to investigate the effects of a non-monetary intervention on transport choices. A GPS-based tracking app records the movements of 814 participants for several months, and automatically detects their travel modes. The treatment consists of sending personalized transport reports to a randomly selected subgroup. These reports contain personalized descriptive and prescriptive information on participants' transport-related external costs. The treatment reduces the climate-related external costs by 5.1% (p=0.05). We find that the treatment effects increase with age and the level of education, and that they decrease with income. Reports with positive prescriptive feedback were correlated with further reductions in external costs, whereas the opposite is true for negative feedback, thus suggesting a ``boomerang effect''. Based on participants' travel response and their willingness-to-pay for future reports, we compute average gross welfare gains of 3.09 Swiss francs per participant and report from a targeted intervention.
papers.reason: Evaluates a micro-level experimental intervention on transport choices in Switzerland with negligible implications for macroeconomic or financial markets.

papers.title: Local shocks and internal migration: The disparate effects of robots and Chinese imports in the US
papers.abstract: Migration is a key mechanism through which local labor markets adjust to economic shocks. In this paper, we analyze the migration response of American workers to two of the most important shocks that hit US manufacturing since the 1990s: Chinese import competition and the introduction of industrial robots. Exploiting plausibly exogenous variation in exposure across US local labor markets over time, we establish a new fact. Even though both shocks drastically reduced employment in the manufacturing sector, only robots led to a sizable decline in population size. We provide evidence that negative employment spillovers outside manufacturing, caused by robots but not by Chinese imports, can explain the different migration responses. We interpret our findings through the lens of a model that highlights two mechanisms: the cost savings that each shock provides and the degree of complementarity between directly and indirectly exposed industries.
papers.reason: It analyzes how U.S. local labor markets adjust via migration to trade and technology shocks, providing background for regional economic trends.

papers.title: Business Cycle Fluctuations and Monetary Policy under Heterogeneous Information
papers.abstract: Modeling business cycle fluctuations and the non-neutrality of money is an ongoing challenge for macroeconomists. This chapter illustrates how higher-order beliefs lead to an overreaction to public information, a mechanism that was introduced by Morris and Shin. It provides technical details to solve a simple class of models based on beauty-contest games. The chapter relates to monetary non-neutrality under heterogeneous information and explains how Woodford initiated the revival of the heterogeneous-information hypothesis by adding strategic complementarities to the model of Lucas. It further discusses the contribution of Mackowiak and Wiederholt and Pasten and Schoenle in rationalizing the limited attention that firms pay to economic shocks. The chapter explains how dispersed information impinges on the transmission of real shocks and business cycle fluctuations. It deals with communication and stabilization policies.
papers.reason: Reviews theoretical literature on heterogeneous information and monetary non-neutrality, offering background rather than actionable empirical findings.

papers.title: Consumption and saving patterns in Switzerland: new evidence based on administrative tax data
papers.abstract: Abstract We use administrative data on income and wealth of taxpayers in the canton of Bern to impute consumption based on the budget constraint. We validate the imputed consumption and use the panel data on consumption, income and wealth to provide stylized facts on consumption and saving patterns in Switzerland for the period 2002-2022. We document a large drop of the saving rate in the first ten years after retirement and show that 75% of permanent income shocks and 40% of transitory income shocks transmit to total consumption expenditures.
papers.reason: Using Swiss administrative panel data, the study delivers granular estimates of marginal propensities to consume and retirement saving drawdown, supporting macro growth and consumer credit analysis.

papers.title: Firm net worth, external finance premia, and monitoring costs: estimates based on firm-level data
papers.abstract: Abstract The sensitivity of the external finance premium to firms’ net-worth-to-capital ratio is central to the strength of the financial accelerator, yet direct firm-level evidence remains scarce. We estimate this elasticity using balance sheet and income statement data for Swiss nonfinancial firms over 1998–2016. To address the endogeneity of net worth, we employ two complementary instrumental variable strategies: one based on firms’ nonoperating income and the other a shift–share design that interacts predetermined exposure to financial income with aggregate dividend returns. Mapping the estimated elasticity into the costly state verification framework as implemented by Bernanke et al. yields structural monitoring costs of about one quarter of firms’ gross return on capital, with estimates ranging from 0.15 to 0.35 across specifications. Our results provide direct firm-level support for the financial accelerator mechanism and imply monitoring costs of the same order of magnitude as the benchmark calibration of Bernanke et al.
papers.reason: Estimates firm-level external finance premia and monitoring costs, supporting corporate credit and financial stability transmission channels.

papers.title: Measuring Euro-Area Inflation Risk with Options: Market-Implied Distribution and Balance of Risks
papers.abstract: We recover risk-neutral spot distributions of euro-area inflation from caps and floors using two non-normal models — the parametric SABR smile and a nonparametric estimator — benchmarked against a normal model. We construct forward distributions from the spot marginals using a copula. Both non-normal models imply skewed and fat-tailed distributions, while the normal benchmark assigns less probability to extreme outcomes. We summarise the distributions with a balance-of-risks index, which varies sharply over short horizons but shows more limited movement over longer horizons. On matched dates, the option-implied balance of risks is generally lower than the corresponding measure reported by professional forecasters.
papers.reason: The study extracts risk-neutral inflation distributions and balance-of-risks indices from euro-area options, directly providing useful pricing and market-expectation metrics for rates and inflation traders.

analysis.summary: This study extracts market-implied probability distributions for euro-area inflation using options contracts, specifically inflation caps and floors. Comparing non-normal modeling approaches—the SABR model and a nonparametric estimator—against a normal benchmark, the author constructs forward distributions using a copula. The non-normal frameworks show that inflation distributions are skewed with fat tails, pricing higher probabilities of extreme inflation outcomes than standard normal models. A derived balance-of-risks index displays significant variation over short horizons but stays more stable over longer horizons. Finally, the option-implied balance of risks is generally lower than comparable expectations recorded in surveys of professional forecasters.
key_takeaways: Non-normal models (SABR and nonparametric) reveal that euro-area inflation option distributions are skewed and fat-tailed, pricing higher probabilities of extreme outcomes than normal benchmarks.
The option-implied balance-of-risks index exhibits sharp variations over short-term horizons, but shows more constrained movement over longer horizons.
Market option-implied balance of inflation risks is generally lower on matched dates compared to the balance of risks reported by professional forecasters.
analysis.relevance: This research provides euro-area inflation and rates strategists with a framework for evaluating tail risks and skewness priced into inflation derivatives. By demonstrating that normal models underestimate extreme inflation outcomes, the paper highlights the necessity of using non-normal pricing models like SABR when extracting market expectations. Additionally, the systematic divergence between option-implied risk measures and survey-based professional forecasts offers a baseline for tracking shifts in risk premia versus consensus surveys over different horizon lengths.
analysis.market_focus_rationale: The paper specifically analyzes euro-area inflation expectations derived from euro-area inflation caps and floors.

papers.title: Replication package for: Cheap to Write, Costly to Run? The Economic and Energy Costs of Model Choice in AI-Assisted Empirical Research
papers.abstract: Replication package of the paper "Cheap to Write, Costly to Run? The Economic and Energy Costs of Model Choice in AI-Assisted Empirical Research" (submitted). Ten AI coding assistants in three price tiers wrote Python scripts for three statistical computations: a latent Dirichlet allocation topic model of 6,000 abstracts, a province-clustered pairs bootstrap for a municipal drought panel, and Monte Carlo permutation Shapley values for a credit default model. Each script was executed on one laptop and graded against the consensus of the frontier assistants of two vendors, and the US cents and scenario watt-hours per valid result were computed over all attempts. The deposit contains the experimental harness and analysis code (MIT), the prompts and reference implementations, the 560 generated scripts with their prompts, token metadata, grades and run metrics, the run records, derived cost and energy tables, numeric run outputs aggregated over documents and loans, the paper's tables, figures and fact sheets (CC BY 4.0), and a script that reproduces the tables and figures offline from the deposited results. The three task data sets are not redistributed except for the part derived from the CC BY 4.0 Combined Drought Indicator; README.md gives their sources, licences and the scripts and sampling rules that rebuild them. AI-generated scripts are provided as generated.
papers.reason: This is a software and energy replication package for AI code generation without direct financial market applications.

papers.title: The AI Investment Boom: Capital Formation, Financing Structures, Interconnections and Vulnerabilities
papers.abstract: This paper examines how the ongoing AI investment cycle is financed and supported, with a focus on the financial and strategic linkages among the main participants in the AI ecosystem. Drawing on a sample of leading firms in the sector, the analysis documents the increasing reliance on private markets to mobilize capital and distribute risk, notably for infrastructure expansion and access to critical components. Particular attention is paid to developments in 2025 and in 2026 to date, with historical data at the group level used to provide context for recent trends. The evidence presented suggests that, while current investment and funding strategies are facilitating rapid capital formation, they may also introduce vulnerabilities associated with long-term commitments, strong interdependencies and the growing use of complex structured arrangements. In this context, the reliance on future cash flows and continued access to external funding and commercial commitments may expose these firms to adverse shocks, especially in a less favorable macro-financial environment.
papers.reason: The study maps the financing structures and funding vulnerabilities of the AI ecosystem, highlighting risks relevant to corporate credit and equity markets.

papers.title: El uso de la inteligencia artificial por parte de las empresas españolas: avances recientes y factores asociados a su uso
papers.abstract: La adopción de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en las empresas españolas ha aumentado de forma significativa entre 2024 y 2026, aunque con gran heterogeneidad. Mientras las pequeñas y medianas empresas mantienen un uso mayoritariamente experimental, las grandes empresas muestran una utilización más intensiva, además de persistir en las diferencias por tamaño y sector. El impacto sobre el empleo es aún limitado, pero ya se observan mejoras en la productividad y la inversión. Las empresas adoptantes destacan por tener mayor productividad, salarios más altos y mayor peso de activos intangibles, lo que refleja la complementariedad con el capital humano cualificado. Los obstáculos a la adopción de la IA varían entre las empresas: entre las no adoptantes predominan las restricciones de recursos y la percepción de baja utilidad, mientras que un grupo más reducido enfrenta barreras técnicas o regulatorias.
papers.reason: The micro-level analysis of Spanish corporate AI adoption provides indirect context on productivity and labor dynamics with limited near-term market application.

papers.title: A Bayesian Analysis of the Cox-Ingersoll-Ross Model
papers.abstract: The Cox-Ingersoll-Ross model (CIR) is a diffusion process with widespread applications in economics, finance and population biology. In this paper we first obtain a full Gibbs Sampler for the exact CIR process observed at equidistant times. We do not require the imposition of the Feller condition. We show how to carry out smoothing and handling of missing data. Additionally, the introduction of a tailored single Metropolis-Hastings step allows us to handle irregular and random time intervals. Secondly, we obtain several asymptotic properties which include Local Asymptotic Normality, consistency and asymptotic normality of conditional maximum likelihood estimation and a Bernstein-von Mises theorem. Lastly, we provide an empirical illustration using U.S. Treasury yields under a variety of priors and a comparison with other models such as the Vasicek and the 3/2 models.
papers.reason: Provides a robust econometric framework for the Cox-Ingersoll-Ross model, empirically illustrated using US Treasury yields.

papers.title: Perspectives on Iberian Economic Integration
papers.abstract: This paper examines the functioning of the European Single Market through the experience of Spain and Portugal, two economies whose geographical proximity, shared border and joint EU membership since 1986 make them a particularly informative case study. Organizing the analysis around the Single Market’s four freedoms, the paper combines descriptive indicators, structural-gravity estimates, a multi-country general-equilibrium trade model, price-convergence and electricity-coupling measures, administrative labour-market data, survival analysis and granular investment and banking data to assess integration in trade, energy, labour mobility and capital markets. The findings show that Iberian integration is substantial but markedly uneven across dimensions. Trade in goods and production network linkages have deepened considerably since accession, and wholesale electricity markets are exceptionally well integrated, reflecting strong complementarities between Spanish solar and Portuguese hydropower generation. By contrast, services trade, labour mobility and non-bank financial investment remain comparatively underdeveloped. These results show that the legal framework of the Single Market has generated deep integration in some markets while leaving others fragmented, and that closing the remaining gaps requires more effective implementation, regulatory cooperation and mutual recognition, supported by infrastructure investment and interoperable administrative systems.
papers.reason: Analyzes trade, energy, and capital market integration in Spain and Portugal, offering useful context on European Single Market dynamics and regional capital flows.

papers.title: Investment irreversibility in a granular world
papers.abstract: We show that investment irreversibility plays a prominent role in shaping aggregate fluctuations in a granular economy, characterized by a fat-tailed distribution of non-atomistic firms. Such an economy satisfies two conditions necessary for irreversibility to matter for aggregate fluctuations: idiosyncratic shocks volatile enough to bind the irreversibility constraint cyclically for a mass of large firms, and a failure of the law of large numbers that prevents firm-level fluctuations from washing out in the aggregate. Through both a direct misallocation channel and an indirect general equilibrium channel, irreversibility dampens the volatility of output, investment, and hours while amplifying the volatility of consumption. Eliminating the friction yields a consumption-equivalent welfare gain of 1.83%; however, merely subsidizing capital liquidation reduces welfare by 0.59%, because firms, compensated by the government, do not internalize the aggregate resource losses and therefore over-disinvest.
papers.reason: The study explores how investment irreversibility in granular economies affects aggregate output and consumption fluctuations, offering insights for capital expenditure cycles.

papers.title: Determinantes de la modalidad del tipo de interés de las hipotecas y evolución de sus márgenes durante el período de endurecimiento de la política monetaria 2022-2023
papers.abstract: En España, durante la última década, las hipotecas a tipo fijo han pasado de ser usadas de manera marginal a ser la modalidad predominante. En este documento se realizan diversos análisis para investigar este fenómeno, cuyos principales resultados son los siguientes. Primero, los factores considerados de oferta parecen tener un mayor poder explicativo que los factores considerados de demanda en la modalidad del tipo hipotecario. Los bancos grandes conceden más hipotecas a tipo fijo, independientemente de la orientación de la política monetaria. Segundo, la relación entre la modalidad de tipo hipotecario y la capacidad de repago del prestatario depende del tono de la política monetaria y el tamaño de las entidades. Mientras que las grandes redujeron su propensión a conceder hipotecas a tipo ajustable (por ejemplo, hipotecas a tipo variable o mixto) a los prestatarios con menor capacidad de repago durante el período de endurecimiento monetario entre 2022 y 2023, las pequeñas no lo hicieron. Finalmente, la evolución de los márgenes medios de las hipotecas varió según su modalidad, el tamaño de las entidades y la orientación de la política monetaria. En las pequeñas —y, aún con mayor intensidad, en las grandes—, el margen medio de las hipotecas a tipo fijo descendió de manera sustancial tras el endurecimiento monetario. En cambio, en las hipotecas a tipo ajustable, los márgenes medios apenas experimentaron cambios, independientemente del tamaño bancario.
papers.reason: Analyzes the shift toward fixed-rate mortgages and bank lending margins in Spain during the 2022-2023 monetary tightening cycle.

papers.title: Locally Robust Inference with Outcomes Predicted by Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Many parameters of interest in economics depend on outcomes generated by machine learning (ML).These generated outcomes are subsequently used in standard econometric estimation and typically treated as observed, a practice that threatens the validity of downstream inference. Empirically relevant cases include dynamic treatment effects under sequential exogeneity, long-term effects with surrogates, the partially linear model with an ML-predicted outcome, productivity persistence with an unrestricted production function and constructed instruments, and outcomes residualized of confounding variation. This paper develops a three-step locally robust GMM framework for valid inference when the dependent variable is generated by ML. We construct a debiased moment condition that augments the identifying moment with first- and second-step influence functions, making inference on the parameter of interest locally insensitive to regularization and model selection biases at both steps. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator and illustrate its finite-sample performance through Monte Carlo simulations. We also apply the method to U.S. mortgage data to study conditional Black--White disparities in a race-blind ML default-risk score. The score predicts subsequent default well overall, but the conditional disparity embedded in the score is much smaller than the corresponding disparity in realized serious delinquency; accounting for first-step estimation also raises the naive out-of-sample estimate of the score disparity.
papers.reason: Develops an econometric methodology for valid inference using machine learning outcomes, illustrated with U.S. mortgage data.

papers.title: Inflation and Price Dispersion: New Cross-Sectoral and International Evidence
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between price dispersion and inflation, shedding light on one major source of the cost of high inflation. By analyzing novel product-level web-scraped data from over 60,000 restaurants and supermarkets across 18 countries facing high and low inflation periods, I uncover new evidence of a significant positive correlation between inflation and price dispersion. My findings reveal that average annualized inflation, ranging between 0 and 20 percentage points across countries within a condensed time frame, is significantly associated with higher price dispersion in both the restaurant and the supermarket sectors. The estimates indicate that the marginal effect of suboptimal inflation on product-level distortions is positive, economically significant in all inflation environments and heterogeneous across sectors. Cross-sectionally, I find that as annualized inflation rises from 0% to 10% inefficient price dispersion is about 46% higher for supermarkets and 73% higher for restaurants. Lastly, the relationship between inflation and price dispersion does not flatten much at higher inflation, so that the marginal cost of additional inflation does not vanish as inflation rises – a pattern standard menu-cost models do not generate. This indicates a sustained impact of inflation on price dispersion, implying that accommodating higher inflation levels incurs substantial welfare costs.
papers.reason: Analyzing multi-country web-scraped data across inflation environments, the paper evaluates welfare costs and price distortions relevant to inflation dynamics and central bank pricing models.

papers.title: The voice as a neurophysiological marker: applications in implicit emotion perception for Neurocash ® and cash design
papers.abstract: Situated within the Neurocash ® framework for measuring implicit emotional and cognitive responses, this review examines the human voice as a non-invasive psychophysiological marker. It outlines the physiological mechanisms of voice production and explains how emotional states influence breathing, vocal-fold vibration and articulation, shaping acoustic features such as pitch and intensity. The review then examines Speech Emotion Recognition as the main approach for extracting emotional information from speech, describing the methodological pipeline from emotional speech databases and preprocessing to classification using traditional machine-learning algorithms and modern deep-learning and self-supervised models. The analysis concludes that no single computational approach is universally optimal, as performance depends on language, emotional categories, data quality and environmental conditions. Overall, this review provides an interdisciplinary framework linking psychophysiology, vocal acoustics and artificial intelligence to support Neurocash ® studies on cognitive workload, perceived security and implicit trust in cash design.
papers.reason: The review focuses on psychophysiological markers and speech emotion recognition for cash design, offering no direct or indirect relevance to financial markets.

papers.title: El proceso de desapalancamiento de las sociedades no financieras españolas en el período 2007-2024
papers.abstract: En este documento se analiza el proceso de desapalancamiento de las sociedades no financieras en España durante el período 2007–2024. Para ello, se explota la granularidad de los datos de la Central de Balances Integrada del Banco de España y se extiende la metodología de DeAngelo, Gonçalves y Stulz (2018) basada en el análisis de la evolución del apalancamiento desde el punto máximo («pico») de cada empresa hasta el mínimo posterior («valle») en el período considerado. Los resultados muestran que la empresa mediana reduce su ratio de deuda sobre los activos del 47 % en el pico al 7 % en el valle consecutivo, que un 31 % de las empresas alcanzan una posición sin deuda en el valle y que un 54 % presentan una posición de liquidez superior al endeudamiento. Para la empresa mediana, este ajuste se completa en un período de tres años y se materializa a través del repago de deuda bancaria y no bancaria. Este proceso presenta una marcada heterogeneidad entre empresas. En particular, el ajuste del apalancamiento es más acusado entre las empresas de menor tamaño y edad, y con mayor probabilidad de impago en el pico de apalancamiento. Dicho ajuste se acompaña de un aumento de la liquidez, una mejora de la rentabilidad y un menor grado de inversión. Por último, se observa una recomposición significativa del pasivo incluso entre las empresas con menores restricciones al crédito bancario. Aunque el análisis no permite distinguir entre los factores de demanda y oferta de crédito, este resultado sugiere que el proceso de desapalancamiento no está impulsado únicamente por restricciones de la oferta de crédito, sino que también refleja decisiones empresariales proactivas. En conjunto, los resultados son coherentes con una estrategia empresarial basada en el uso de los recursos internos para reducir el endeudamiento, reforzar la posición de liquidez y aumentar la flexibilidad financiera.
papers.reason: Using granular balance sheet data on Spanish firms from 2007 to 2024, the paper evaluates corporate debt reduction and balance sheet adjustments relevant to credit analysis.

papers.title: Land concentration and large renewable energy projects
papers.abstract: This paper examines how land ownership concentration shapes the deployment of large-scale renewable energy projects across six European countries (Spain, Germany, France, Italy, Belgium and the Netherlands). Using a 5×5 km grid-cell framework with cadastral parcel data, we show that cells with a higher share of area in large parcels (= 10 ha) are substantially more likely to host mega photovoltaic (PV) plants (= 50 ha), with a standardized semi-elasticity of 68% in the pooled sample, consistent across all six countries. Land concentration also drives aggregate solar deployment: a one-standard-deviation increase raises expected PV hectares within a grid cell by 62%, an effect driven almost entirely by the mega-plant margin. By contrast, the effect on wind parks is weaker and heterogeneous, consistent with wind requiring less contiguous land assembly than solar. A specificity test and decomposition analysis corroborate that the assembly mechanism operates specifically at the mega-plant margin, and a horse race between cadastral concentration and farm operational size establishes that ownership, not farming scale, is the operative mechanism. A finer 500 m grid within-municipality analysis corroborates the effect of land concentration on mega PV plants and further reveals that it is attenuated in irrigated areas, where higher agricultural rents raise landowner reservation values. We rationalize these patterns with a conceptual framework in which solar assembly requires unanimous consent from a set of landowners whose number falls with parcel size, while wind requires only a subset. Our findings reveal that land ownership structure is a decisive factor in the energy transition: fragmentation impedes large-scale deployment, while concentration enables it but channels its benefits toward a few large landowners, potentially deepening rural grievances and local opposition.
papers.reason: Investigates how land ownership concentration affects large-scale solar project deployment across six European countries, informing structural drivers of the green transition.

papers.title: Regional convergence dynamics in the main European economies
papers.abstract: This paper examines the convergence dynamics of GDP per capita across 98 regions in Spain, Germany, France and Italy over the period 1998-2025. Using the methodology developed by Phillips and Sul (2007, 2009), six convergence clubs are identified. The results reveal substantial structural heterogeneity: the most advanced clubs, composed primarily of German regions, present GDP per capita levels that are persistently above the sample average. Intermediate and lower-income clubs, consisting mainly of French, Italian and Spanish regions, converge towards lower relative income equilibria. To estimate the determinants of regional growth, a heterogeneous dynamic panel model with common effects is used. The findings suggest that regional disparities across Europe reflect not only differences in factor endowments, but also differences in the regions’ ability to transform these endowments into economic growth. In particular, human capital and physical capital stock emerge as key factors in explaining these divergences.
papers.reason: Identifies six regional convergence clubs across major European economies and links structural disparities to human and physical capital, offering background for European sovereign credit.

papers.title: Political Polarization and Legislative Gridlock: A Comparative High-Frequency Approach
papers.abstract: We propose a narrative-based approach to construct high-frequency measures of political polarization and legislative gridlock for seven democracies: France, Germany, Spain, Italy, the UK, the U.S., and Canada. Our indices reveal that polarization has risen markedly since the Global Financial and Sovereign Debt Crises, with a faster increase in North America than in Europe. Through a range of exercises we show that the two indices respond differently to elections and unified government control, and that the latter weakens the pass-through between political polarization and gridlock. Consistent with literature, we also find that investment declines following an increase in either index. Together, these high-frequency, cross-country measures provide a new tool for comparative political economy.
papers.reason: Constructs high-frequency measures of political polarization and legislative gridlock across seven advanced economies, noting negative impacts on investment.

papers.title: The Macroeconomic Effects of Defence Expenditure: Evidence from Spain
papers.abstract: We estimate the macroeconomic effects of defence expenditure using a novel dataset covering the universe of defence procurement contracts in Spain over 30 years. Our defence procurement data overcomes identification challenges posed by implementation lags inherent in traditional government spending, as contracts are awarded years before production begins and spending is recorded in government national accounts only upon delivery. Using local projections, we find that GDP effects take time to materialise, become sizeable, but remain transitory. That is, while defence investment has relevant economic consequences, these are bound to occur in the medium run insofar as the spending process is hindered by implementation lags. A DSGE model calibrated to our empirical setting yields two main findings. First, reducing implementation lags to US levels would meaningfully frontload the macroeconomic effects. Second, defence spending delivers more transient and smaller long-run effects than general public investment projects.
papers.reason: Evaluates the macroeconomic and GDP effects of defence expenditure using Spanish procurement data, offering insights relevant to European fiscal outlooks.

papers.title: A New Keynesian Model of the Term Structures of Equity and Bond Returns
papers.abstract: A simple production economy with nominal price rigidities explains several key asset pricing facts, including the average slopes and cyclicality of equity and interest rate term structures. Nominal rigidities amplify the procyclicality of dividends after negative productivity shocks and generate countercyclical inflation, as sluggish price adjustment leads to a gradual dividend recovery. Consequently, short-duration equities (bonds) have more (less) procyclical payoffs than their long-duration counterparts. Slow-moving consumption habits produce large, countercyclical risk prices, yielding realistic asset valuations. Extending Campbell-Cochrane preferences with both market and home consumption habits allows them to operate in production economies while preserving realistic macroeconomic dynamics.
papers.reason: Develops a New Keynesian model explaining the term structures and cyclicality of both equity and bond returns, directly informing fixed income and equity strategists.

papers.title: Game changer? Impact of a multi-component reading intervention on cognitive and socioemotional skills
papers.abstract: Abstract We evaluate a holistic reading intervention involving 527 third-grade students in Chilean schools catering to disadvantaged populations. The intervention features an adaptive computer game designed to identify and improve weaknesses in literacy and cognitive skills, and is complemented by a mobile library and advice to parents aimed at fostering student engagement and parental involvement. Leveraging a matched-pair design under the staggered implementation of the intervention, in which we retrospectively match five schools already scheduled to receive the treatment with five schools from the yet-to-be-selected pool, we assess its impacts on both cognitive and socioemotional outcomes. Treated students are 10–30% of a standard deviation more likely to have higher academic aspirations, to believe that their performance is better than that of their peers, and that courses are easy. We also find suggestive evidence of a more internal locus of control and of improvements in performance on a nation-wide, standardized language test, indicating that a short, light-touch, and cost-effective bundled program can improve socioemotional outcomes and, potentially, reading performance.
papers.reason: Evaluates a reading intervention for students in Chile with negligible direct relevance to financial markets.

papers.title: Power, inclusion and the role of SMEs in European public procurement
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) participation in European public procurement, aiming to understand disparities across member states despite harmonised EU Directives. Design/methodology/approach Using a novel dataset of 839,778 tenders with information about SME participation from the Tenders Electronic Daily (TED) platform covering 29 countries from 2018 to 2023, we analyse SME participation rates, contract award shares, and geographic competition patterns. Findings Significant variation is observed: Eastern European countries exceed 80% SME participation, while several Western European countries remain below 40%. SMEs participate in about 80% of tenders but secure only 40–60% of contract values. Geographic proximity enhances SME competitiveness in local markets, especially for contracts under €500,000. Institutional and administrative factors appear more decisive than regulatory frameworks alone. Research limitations/implications Limitations include potential data quality issues. However, these were mitigated where possible, and the database remains the only available offering comparable data across Europe. Future research should explore institutional and cultural factors in greater depth through country-level studies. Practical implications Policymakers should adopt tailored approaches addressing administrative complexity and regional market conditions, simplifying procedures and improving data transparency to boost SME inclusion. Social implications Identifying ways to promote SME participation can support corrective actions that foster economic inclusion and strengthen local entrepreneurship across the EU. Originality/value This study provides new empirical evidence on the “implementation paradox” in EU public procurement, highlighting the need for context-specific strategies to enhance SME inclusion.
papers.reason: Examines SME participation in European public procurement across 29 countries, offering microeconomic insights into regional market conditions.

papers.title: AI-signaling premium in economics and finance research
papers.abstract: Citations to AI-related work may reflect both content and presentation. Using 30,114 Scopus articles published in 2021-2025, this paper examines whether AI signaling in titles, abstracts, or keywords predicts citations. AI signaling is measured in two stages: a dictionary identifies the articles carrying an AI term, and a large language model classifies each one by whether AI is the subject studied or the method applied. Controlling for journal and year fixed effects, readability, topic shares, and author heterogeneity, we find a positive association concentrated in titles. Title-visible mentions are associated with about 60% more citations than papers with no AI signal, and about 43% more than papers that mention AI only in the keywords. Title visible articles are cited more than unsignaled ones whether AI is the method a paper uses or the subject it studies. Set against other heavily cited trends, the gap between title and keywords is of the same size for ESG and absent for crypto-assets and COVID-19. The result holds with author fixed effects, author-quality controls, count models, and comparison inside the same journal issue. The pattern is consistent with limited attention, under which the position of a label carries information about where to look.
papers.reason: Examines citation premiums for AI-related research titles without direct implications for financial markets or macroeconomic policy.

papers.title: Flooded by China? Trade diversion due to US tariffs during Trump’s first mandate
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether US tariffs on China diverted Chinese exports towards the EU, exploiting the first US-China trade war as a setting that permits clean identification of trade diversion effects. Applying difference-in-differences local projections to highly disaggregated tariff, import and unit value data, it shows that trade diversion occurred but was limited in size. For each dollar reduction in US imports from China, 9 cents were redirected to the EU market in real terms. The effects varied substantially across products and destination markets. Trade diversion was strongest for complex capital goods and homogeneous intermediate inputs, and was more pronounced in EU markets with greater import exposure to China and weaker competition from alternative suppliers. Products experiencing effective diversion also exhibited significant price declines, with competitive pressures concentrated in lower-price market segments. These findings suggest that tariffs of a magnitude comparable to those imposed by the United States in 2025 could redirect Chinese exports towards the EU, potentially contributing to a second “China shock” in Europe. While the aggregate effects are modest, diversion and price pressures may be considerably stronger in specific product categories and destination markets.
papers.reason: Provides empirical estimates of trade diversion from US-China tariffs into the EU, relevant for European trade flows and sector-specific competitive pressures.

papers.title: Politización y burocratización. El doble reto de la calidad institucional en España
papers.abstract: Este artículo analiza la calidad institucional en España a partir de dos desequilibrios interrelacionados: los excesos de burocratización y de politización que padecen las Administraciones públicas. En primer lugar, se señalan los notables efectos que tiene la calidad de gobierno —definida no por la cantidad de servicios públicos prestados, sino por la implementación imparcial, eficaz y no corrupta de los mismos— sobre el bienestar de una comunidad. A continuación, el artículo examina la tensión entre legalidad y gestión, subrayando el peso histórico de la tradición legalista española, que dificulta la puesta en marcha de iniciativas de modernización en la gestión pública. Los controles procedimentales ex ante se imponen a los controles de resultados ex post. Por su parte, la gestión de recursos humanos es, a la vez, demasiado rígida en niveles intermedios y demasiado volátil y politizada en los niveles superiores. Esta combinación no genera los incentivos adecuados ni para la innovación ni para la prevención de abusos.
papers.reason: Discusses bureaucratic and political challenges in Spanish public administration with only indirect macroeconomic relevance.

papers.title: Moving Out: Geoeconomic Policy and the Relocation of Foreign Affiliates
papers.abstract: Governments increasingly use trade and industrial policy to reshape where multinationals produce, yet standard measures of this geoeconomic pressure are aggregate and cannot detect origin-specific discrimination. We build a bilateral, directional index of relative protectionism that measures how restrictive a destination is toward a given origin. We combine it with bilateral geopolitical risk indices and global ownership links over the period 2010-21, and estimate a gravity-type Poisson-Pseudo Maximum Likelihood model with three-way fixed effects. Our results show that where bilateral protectionism is greater, foreign-affiliate presence is markedly smaller: a 1 percentage point increase in the index is associated with 1.3% fewer subsidiaries than that origin-destination pair would otherwise have. The main mechanism runs through an operational hostility channel (e.g. discriminatory subsidies, procurement exclusion), which outweighs an offsetting tariff-jumping channel and concentrates in non-tradable sectors, where serving the market requires local presence. The estimates show no evidence of anticipation and are robust to longer lags and sample splits. Bilateral geopolitical risk enters with the same negative sign, adding a smaller but complementary layer of fragmentation risk to the effect of geoeconomic policy.
papers.reason: Constructs a bilateral protectionism index to evaluate how geoeconomic policy and geopolitical risk drive the relocation of foreign multinational affiliates.

papers.title: Measuring Merger Effects with Revenue Data
papers.abstract: We study how revenue productivity (TFPR) and markups evolve after mergers across the economy. In financial-statement data, targets cease to exist as reporting entities after a deal, so tracking the merged firm requires constructing the combined acquirer-target unit before the merger. We formalize the biases that arise without this correction and implement it across 3,759 horizontal mergers in Spain between 1997 and 2022. Revenue productivity rises by approximately 4% within eight years and markups by approximately 5% to 6%. The breakdown by industry reveals that revenue productivity gains are broad-based, while markup increases are concentrated. Most industries show modest markup effects of 3% or less, with the largest increases occurring in two industries accounting for a small share of deals, led by human health activities. We find that without the boundary correction, both estimated effects reverse sign. The results suggest that mergers tend to raise the revenue productivity of the combined firm across the board, consistent with operational improvements, while large markup increases are a feature of specific industries rather than a general consequence of consolidation.
papers.reason: Examines the evolution of revenue productivity and markups following corporate mergers using Spanish firm-level data, offering microeconomic insights into pricing power.

papers.title: Navigating Climate Risk for Resilience: A Roadmap of Research Patterns and Emerging Trends
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Climate risk has become a defining challenge for business strategy, yet its research landscape remains fragmented across disciplines. This study maps the intellectual structure of climate risk research through a bibliometric analysis enriched with latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) topic modeling of 2715 peer‐reviewed articles. Our analysis first identifies the following six consolidated research patterns: (1) climate adaptation and community resilience, (2) climate risk and insurance mechanisms, (3) climate finance and green investment, (4) climate extremes and scenario modeling, (5) climate impacts and agricultural resilience, and (6) climate mitigation and energy transition. Analysis of the 2020–2024 literature reveals four emerging trends: urban climate adaptation, climate risk and financial stability, extreme climate events and climate modeling, agriculture, food security and household security. The findings indicate a shift toward integrated approaches connecting the physical, social, and financial dimensions of climate risk. The resulting roadmap identifies converging risks and strategic priorities for organizational resilience while providing policymakers with an evolving evidence base to support climate governance and informed decision‐making under deepening uncertainty.
papers.reason: A bibliometric mapping of climate risk research literature, providing a high-level overview of academic trends rather than direct market pricing or analytical tools.

papers.title: Geopolitical shocks and household financial distress in Europe: The Russia–Ukraine war
papers.abstract: This paper examines the impact of a major geopolitical risk shock, comparable in scale to the outbreak of the Russia–Ukraine war, on household financial distress in five European countries. We combine a VAR, household survey data, and theoretical insights to develop macro–micro simulations that quantify how such shocks influence household balance sheets. The VAR traces the macroeconomic effects of a surge in geopolitical risk, which we apply to household-level data using the HFCS. We find the shock is associated with elevated inflation, tighter monetary policy, higher mortgage rates, and falling house prices. Our simulations show these dynamics significantly increase financial distress, with variation across countries. We incorporate endogenous consumption responses and show that adjustments driven by interest rate exposure, inflation, and housing wealth play a key role in shaping household resilience. We also document that younger and lower-income households tend to increase consumption following the shock, exacerbating their financial vulnerability.
papers.reason: Quantifies the impact of geopolitical risk shocks on European household balance sheets through inflation, higher mortgage rates, and falling house prices.

papers.title: The Intangible Economy
papers.abstract: The paper explores how a small low-tax economy is affected by foreign corporate-tax shocks. To address this question, I develop a dynamic general-equilibrium model, in which multinational firms engage in both tangible and intangible FDI. Intangible assets arise from multinationals' R&D activities. Each multinational decides whether to place its intangibles in the parent firm or in an overseas affiliate. The placement decision shapes the intra-firm trade in royalties and R&D services. The model reveals that corporate taxes can directly impact arm's-length prices of multinational firms. I investigate territorial corporate taxation as well as worldwide taxation of intangible income.
papers.reason: The paper models how foreign corporate-tax shocks and multinational intangible asset placement affect intra-firm trade and pricing.

papers.title: Which Text Matters: Handling Model Uncertainty in Text-as-Data Regressions, with an Application to Central Bank Communication
papers.abstract: Social scientists routinely convert text into covariates like topic shares, ideal points or sentiment scores, and insert them into statistical models of interest. This two-step design is convenient, but it is rarely guided by theory: little tells the analyst which text-based covariates to construct or include. Each approach embodies contestable measurement choices, and competing operationalizations of the same construct can support different conclusions, so a single research question gives rise to a menu of competing regression models. Which text constructed covariates belong in a model, and in what functional form, is thus a problem of model uncertainty. We propose spike-and-slab generalized additive models (SSGAMs), which jointly select covariates and determine whether their effects are linear or nonlinear. We illustrate the approach with the communication of a powerful unelected institution, asking which of 45 competing text indicators from 224 monthly European Central Bank press conferences, spanning late 2002 to mid-2025, track professional inflation expectations. A sparse set is selected; widely used alternatives, and every tested nonlinear effect, carry no incremental information.
papers.reason: It offers a methodological framework for handling text-as-data model uncertainty, applied to ECB press conferences and inflation expectations.

papers.title: The Depositary of Last Resort
papers.abstract: Abstract What are the consequences of making central bank deposits accessible to actors beyond the banking sector? We collect novel micro data on deposit accounts historically held with the Bank of England by individuals and firms other than banks to study their role in the financial panic of 1866. We document that the use of deposit accounts at the central bank soared during the crisis, while commercial banks permanently lost funding. The expansion in the number of active accounts was fueled by individuals, but the intensive margin increase in balances came almost entirely from firms. Recourse to central bank deposits was heterogeneous and persisted well beyond the panic, reflecting easy access, low opportunity costs, and positive network externalities. At the same time, retail borrowers seeking liquidity support from the Bank during the crisis preferred receiving loan proceeds in the form of cash rather than deposits. JEL Classification: E58, G01, G11, G20, N13, N23
papers.reason: Using historical micro data on non-bank access to Bank of England deposits during the 1866 panic, the paper offers indirect insights for modern debates on central bank digital currencies and financial stability.

papers.title: The share of housing wealth and the decline in real interest rates
papers.abstract: Abstract The share of housing in private wealth has risen substantially across advanced economies over recent decades, alongside a near doubling of aggregate wealth‐to‐income ratios. On closer inspection, this global trend masks substantial regional disparities. While the housing wealth share changed little in the USA, it increased sharply in the larger European economies. This paper asks whether a standard asset‐pricing framework can account for these facts in light of the secular decline in interest rates. Comparing steady states calibrated to 1980 and 2017, I show that lower discount rates raise aggregate wealth only modestly, and leave the housing share essentially unchanged, because they capitalize housing and non‐housing income streams in roughly equal proportion. Matching the data requires two further mechanisms: an increase in markups, which lifts firm valuations through the present value of monopoly profits, and the presence of outright owners, which makes aggregate housing wealth more sensitive to house‐price increases by limiting offsetting quantity adjustments. Closed‐form expressions and a numerical calibration show that the interaction of these channels can reproduce both the global rise in the housing share and the USA–Europe divergence: in the USA, rising markups dominate, whereas in Europe, the expansion of outright ownership plays the central role.
papers.reason: Analyzes how the secular decline in interest rates and rising markups drive housing wealth shares and regional divergence in advanced economies.

papers.title: Are there asymmetries in euro area monetary policy transmission?
papers.abstract: We answer the question posed in the title with a nonlinear mixed-frequency vector autoregression, estimated with Bayesian additive regression trees. The model combines monthly macro-financial variables with quarterly bank lending survey data, and identifies the dynamic responses from high-frequency policy surprises. Sign asymmetry dominates; a tightening produces monetary policy transmission mostly in line with the theoretical predictions, whereas easing of any size produces mostly insignificant responses. Peak effects vary with initial conditions, while several common, predefined regime splits do not yield considerable differences in the propagation of the shocks.
papers.reason: Directly informs euro area rate expectations and yield curve dynamics by demonstrating asymmetric transmission where monetary tightening produces significant effects while easing does not.

papers.title: Jenseits des Gesamtwachstums: Russlands uneinheitliche Kriegswirtschaft
papers.abstract: Seit der groß angelegten Invasion in die Ukraine zeigt die russische Wirtschaft je nach Sektor uneinheitliche Entwicklungen.Dieser Artikel untersucht anhand von Statistiken zur russischen Industrie und zu Unternehmensgewinnen diese Unterschiede.In den mit dem Militär verbundenen Sektoren sind sowohl die Produktion als auch die Gewinne stark gestiegen, während viele zivile Industriezweige mit Produktionsrückgängen, geringeren Gewinnen und höheren Kosten zu kämpfen haben.Selbst innerhalb einzelner Branchen zeigen detaillierte Daten auf Produktebene erhebliche Schwankungen.Die Ergebnisse deuten darauf hin, dass sich das Wachstum Russlands in Kriegszeiten zunehmend konzentriert, was es immer schwieriger macht, das Wachstum aufrechtzuerhalten.
papers.reason: Analyzes sectoral divergence in Russia's wartime economy using industry and corporate profit data.

papers.title: Shareholder conflicts, institutional quality, and tax avoidance
papers.abstract: Abstract This study combines institutional theory with the logic of mixed gambles to examine how disproportionate voting rights of majority shareholders influence corporate tax behavior in the institutional context of China. We find support for our theoretical prediction that disproportionate voting rights create greater incentive for tax avoidance in China. Moreover, we leverage the heterogeneity in institutional strength across China to explicitly examine the role of institutions in shaping the relationship between disproportionate voting rights and tax avoidance. Our study extends agency research on minority shareholder expropriation by showing that when disproportionate voting rights co-exist with institutional voids, greater costs are imposed on minority shareholders and on society in the form of lower tax revenue for social investment. Practically, our findings can help inform the regulatory debates about the societal consequences of corporate structuring mechanisms (dual class shares and pyramid ownership) that enable disproportionate voting rights and give dominant shareholders outsized control over corporate resources. Our results also advance knowledge regarding the consequences of weaker institutional environments for minority shareholders and society more broadly.
papers.reason: Analyzes how disproportionate voting rights influence corporate tax avoidance in China, offering insights relevant to emerging market governance.

papers.title: Corporate Financial Constraints, Minimum Wage Policies, and Employment
papers.abstract: Abstract We examine how corporate financial constraints shape firms’ employment responses to minimum wage policies. Exploiting the federal minimum wage increase during the financial crisis and variation in firms’ debt maturity structures at the crisis onset, we find that financially constrained firms significantly reduce employment. To assess external validity, we analyze staggered state-level minimum wage increases over time. Consistent with the crisis evidence, employment declines in establishments of constrained firms, whereas unconstrained firms expand in areas with a larger supply of minimum-wage workers and higher turnover. Our results highlight the central role of financial constraints in mediating labor policy effects.
papers.reason: The empirical findings show how corporate debt maturity and financial constraints mediate employment responses to minimum wage hikes, informing credit risk and corporate research.

papers.title: Employee Approval of CEOs and Debt Market Outcomes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We examine whether employee‐based assessments of CEO quality convey value‐relevant information to debt markets. Using over half a million Glassdoor employee reviews from 2012 to 2018, matched to corporate bond issuance data for US firms, we study the relation between employee approval of CEOs and firms’ credit ratings and borrowing costs. We find that higher CEO approval predicts higher bond credit ratings and significantly lower at‐issue yield spreads, with the strongest formal cross‐sectional evidence among speculative‐grade issuers and directionally consistent evidence among smaller and highly leveraged issuers. The bond‐spread relation remains significant after controlling for firm and bond characteristics, firm fixed effects, and overall employee satisfaction, and we provide complementary evidence using orthogonalized CEO approval, instrumental variables, and change regressions. We further show that CEO approval mitigates increases in debt financing costs during the COVID‐19 crisis. Overall, our findings indicate that employee assessments of top executives provide incremental, priced information about firm risk that is incorporated into credit market outcomes.
papers.reason: Demonstrates that employee assessments of CEOs contain priced risk information that predicts credit ratings and bond yield spreads for US firms.

papers.title: Replication material for: The incidence of rent subsidies: Evidence on rents, housing choices and supply
papers.abstract: This paper asks whether, and under which circumstances, rent subsidies to low-income households increase rents. We study a reform of the Finnish housing allowance system that caused large quasi-random variation in housing allowances. Using register data spanning five years before and after the reform, we find that large increases in allowances for affected housing units had little or no effect on their rents relative to other units. The effect of a one-euro increase in housing allowance on rent is roughly 0.036 euros with a standard error of 0.028. We provide novel evidence on the underlying demand- and supply-side responses that drive the rent effects. The reform led to only small changes in recipients’ housing choices, and at most modest changes in rental supply. Our interpretation is that rent subsidies can be effective in helping recipient households even in supply-constrained contexts, if recipients’ housing choices are unresponsive to the subsidy.
papers.reason: Using Finnish administrative data, the paper evaluates the impact of rent subsidies on rental prices and housing choices, offering relevant insights for housing economics and urban policy.

papers.title: The role of ecotourism in regional environmental transformation: evidence from Chinese cities
papers.abstract: Purpose This study evaluates whether city-level ecotourism certification can function as an effective indirect environmental policy instrument by reducing industrial pollution. It further identifies the channels through which such effects arise, and derives targeted implications for regional policy design. Design/methodology/approach We use the introduction of China's Prototype-zone of National Ecotourism Attractions (PNEA) pilot program as a quasi-natural experiment and employ a staggered difference-in-differences approach on panel data from 296 Chinese cities covering the period from 2007 to 2019. Findings We find that PNEA certification significantly reduces industrial pollution, particularly in reducing wastewater and sulfur dioxide emissions. The mechanisms driving this effect are the promotion of green technological innovation and an amplifying effect of digitalization on green industrial development. Originality/value This study is among the most comprehensive ones to directly link ecotourism to industrial emissions reduction, highlighting the potential role of ecotourism as a tool for regional sustainable development. By documenting structural effects on pollution and identifying innovation and digitalization as key enabling factors, the study offers actionable guidance for integrating ecotourism certification into broader environmental policy frameworks.
papers.reason: Evaluates ecotourism certification as an environmental policy instrument using Chinese city-level data, offering micro-level sectoral insights with indirect macroeconomic and policy implications.

papers.title: DOES CLIMATE TRANSITION RISK UNDERMINE BANKS’ LOAN PORTFOLIO? EVIDENCE FROM BANK SUPERVISORY MICRO DATASET
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use a unique micro dataset on households and nonfinancial corporations to assess the impact of climate transition risks on banks’ loan portfolios. We estimate this effect by incorporating scenarios and macroeconomic projections from the Network for Greening the Financial System into the central bank’s risk-assessment framework. We find that a smooth transition away from emission-intensive sectors results in minimal credit losses for banks. In contrast, an uneven transition can lead to significantly higher losses, sometimes exceeding those from worst-case nonclimate scenarios. The results are sensitive to rising energy prices and to increased default rates in emission-intensive sectors. These findings provide valuable insights for small, open, and emission-intensive economies with bank-based financial sectors, such as Slovakia.
papers.reason: Evaluates the impact of climate transition scenarios on bank loan portfolios using supervisory micro data, offering insights for banking stability.

papers.title: FinTech development and bank credit risk: Spatial spillovers and the role of financial system structures
papers.abstract: Rapid FinTech development is reshaping global financial systems, yet the understanding of its implications for the level of risk undertaken by banks remains ambiguous. This study examines the relationship between FinTech development and credit risk in the banking sector across 63 countries from 2013 to 2021. We distinguish between bank-based and market-based financial system structures, as well as between financially developed and underdeveloped economies within these two structures. Furthermore, we employ spatial models to account for cross-border spillovers in bank risk and adopt a novel measure of FinTech development that is based on FinTech investment activities. Our findings first reveal the existence of positive spatial dependence in bank credit risk across countries, highlighting the necessity of spatial analysis. Second, using the Spatial Durbin Model, which provides the best fit for our data, we show that FinTech development reduces bank credit risk both domestically and internationally. Third, such credit risk-mitigating effect of FinTech is concentrated in bank-based financial systems, whereas it is absent in market-based structures. Fourth, within bank-based economics, this effect is more pronounced in financially underdeveloped countries compared with those with well-developed financial markets. Finally, our robustness checks support these findings. This paper highlights FinTech’s potential in mitigating bank credit risk and underscores the importance of considering financial structures and spatial interdependence in assessing bank risk.
papers.reason: Analyzes cross-border spillovers and the mitigating effect of FinTech on bank credit risk across 63 countries, supporting banking sector credit analysis.

papers.title: Correcting for Nonignorable Nonresponse Bias in Ordinal Observational Survey Data
papers.abstract: Abstract Many political surveys rely on post-stratification, raking or related weighting adjustments to align respondents with the target population. But when respondents differ from nonrespondents on the outcome itself (nonignorable nonresponse), these adjustments can fail, introducing bias even into basic descriptives. We provide a practical method that corrects for nonignorable nonresponse by leveraging response-propensity proxies (e.g., a respondent’s rating of the interview or interviewer-coded cooperativeness) observed among respondents to extrapolate toward nonrespondents, while directly integrating observable covariates and retaining the benefits of post-stratification with known population shares. The method generalizes the variable-response-propensity framework of Peress (2010) from binary to ordinal outcomes, which are widely used to measure trust, satisfaction and policy attitudes. The resulting estimator is computed by maximum likelihood and implemented in a compact R routine that handles both ordinal and binary outcomes. Using the 2024 American National Election Study, we show that accounting for nonignorable nonresponse produces substantively meaningful shifts for life satisfaction (estimated latent correlation ρ ≈ 0.47 $\rho \approx 0.47$ rho almost equals 0.47 ), while yielding only modest changes for retrospective economic evaluations ( ρ ≈ 0.14 $\rho \approx 0.14$ rho almost equals 0.14 ), highlighting when nonignorable nonresponse substantively affects survey estimates.
papers.reason: Proposes a statistical method to correct for nonresponse bias in political and social survey data, lacking direct macro-financial or market applications.

papers.title: Finančna pismenost in investicijske odločitve posameznika
papers.abstract: POVZETEKMagistrska naloga preučuje povezavo finančne pismenosti z investicijskimi odločitvami posameznikov v Sloveniji.S pomočjo anketnega vprašalnika je bilo raziskano, kako različni demografski in ekonomski dejavniki, kot so starost, spol, izobrazba in ekonomski položaj, vplivajo na naložbeno strategijo posameznikov, razpršenost portfelja ter pripravljenost na sprejemanje tveganj.Ugotovitve so pokazale, da višja finančna pismenost spodbuja bolj razpršene naložbe, večjo pripravljenost na tveganje in posledično dolgoročno stabilnost donosov.V sklepnem delu so podani predlogi za uvedbo finančnega izobraževanja v šolski sistem in na delovna mesta, s poudarkom na mladih, ženskah ter posameznikih z nižjimi dohodki.
