papers.title: Syrona: an open-source visual analytics tool for pairwise comparison of health datasets in OMOP CDM
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Health research increasingly relies on observational datasets that capture systematically different patient populations, affecting the representativeness, comparability, and transportability of study findings. Yet these differences are rarely quantified across clinical domains or explored interactively, and the workflow for pairwise dataset comparison remains fragmented. No existing OHDSI tool provides an integrated visual analytics workflow for exploratory pairwise comparison of concept prevalence patterns between datasets on the OMOP Common Data Model. Results We present Syrona, an open-source visual analytics tool for systematic pairwise comparison of datasets and subcohorts on the OMOP Common Data Model. Syrona extracts annual prevalence for conditions, procedures, and drugs from any OMOP CDM database, computes prevalence ratios across demographic strata, and synthesizes them via multilevel meta-analysis. A coordinated dashboard - distributional overviews, stratified heatmaps, forest plots, and absolute prevalence comparisons - enables interactive exploration driven by domain-adaptive SNOMED CT and ATC filtering. Three case studies on Estonian national health data (495,000 persons, 2012–2024) demonstrate how the tool supports representativeness assessment, institutional practice comparison, and coding artifact detection. Conclusions Syrona is open-source and applicable to any OMOP CDM database. By treating dataset comparison as a visual analytics problem rather than a tabular reporting task, it addresses a gap in the OHDSI ecosystem and supports systematic assessment of datasets in distributed observational research.
papers.reason: The paper introduces an open-source visual analytics tool for comparing health datasets and clinical prevalence, with no relevance to financial markets.

papers.title: FinTech ecosystem effectiveness: Balancing competitiveness, profitability, innovation and resilience — The case of Latvia
papers.abstract: This paper examines Latvia’s FinTech ecosystem as a case of small-market adaptation to technology-driven change in the financial sector. It develops and applies an Ecosystem Effectiveness Model that connects enabling capacities (technological readiness, institutional collaboration, regulatory environment and market adoption) with outcome dimensions of competitiveness, profitability, innovation and resilience. The study draws on a bibliometric mapping of FinTech research and on micro-level evidence from the 2025 Bank of Latvia Innovation Survey, using principal component analysis, cluster analysis and logistic regression to profile ecosystem actors and their innovation behaviour. The results demonstrate that Latvia has achieved relatively high Application Programming Interface penetration, growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in compliance and analytics, and structured FinTech– bank cooperation, supported by innovation-oriented regulation and access to payment infrastructure. At the same time, gaps in deep-tech scaling, venture capital availability, talent and international promotion could limit improvements in ecosystem performance. By situating Latvia’s experience within broader European FinTech dynamics, the paper demonstrates how small economies can design policy and governance arrangements to convert ‘secondgeneration disruptors’ (eg AI, tokenisation) into focused, resilient specialisation paths rather than scale-based competition. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.
papers.reason: Examines Latvia's FinTech sector using micro-level survey data, offering only indirect insights for broader European banking or tech trends.

papers.title: Real GDP Forecasts by International Organisations
papers.abstract: We study forecasts for real gross domestic product growth by international organisations. These forecasts influence policy decisions by international organisations and national governments, and receive significant attention from the private sector. First, we compare the accuracy of forecasters and test the rationality of forecasts using a large dataset of forecasts by four international organisations (the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, the European Commission and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) and private-sector forecasts. Second, we derive a new decomposition of differences in forecast accuracy into contributions from disagreement and the accuracy of the average forecast. Finally, we present theoretical results and empirical evidence on two explanations for the rejection of forecast rationality: the use of conditioning assumptions and the practice of making modal forecasts.
papers.reason: It evaluates GDP forecast accuracy and rationality across major international organizations compared to private-sector forecasts.

papers.title: Technological Transformation Research: Thematic Evolution Analysis With Consistent Impact Rank Aggregation (CIRA)
papers.abstract: We analyse the evolving literature on technological transformation (1966–2021), offering a systematic and holistic overview of its multi-dimensional and multi-level nature. Using bibliographic performance analysis, science mapping, and thematic evolution analysis, we map the field’s intellectual structure and thematic development. To strengthen performance evaluation of themes, we introduce Consistent Impact Rank Aggregation (CIRA), a conceptually novel, parametric rank-based method with an explicit and adaptable consistency filter, designed to highlight recurrent top-performing units across multiple metrics. Our findings reveal a unifying contemporary structure of the technological transformation field comprising two core streams: (i) firm-level technological capabilities development and learning processes for competitive advantage and catching up in latecomer firms, and (ii) technological upgrading and convergence through knowledge spillovers at national and sectoral levels. Over three decades (1991–2021), the field has evolved through exploratory, expansion, consolidation, and convergence phases, gradually integrating fragmented research into a more cohesive and conceptually mature body of knowledge. This process is marked by increasing thematic convergence, evolving content and importance of themes, and shifting conceptual drivers. In the convergence phase (2016–2021), the technological transformation centres on innovation and technological change topics, with emerging emphasis on technology upgrading and innovation policy, specialisation in Industry 4.0-led technological performance, and is driven by technology diffusion, technological capabilities, and dynamic capabilities themes. CIRA results further confirm that the field’s adaptive core has been consistently sustained by technology diffusion, technological capabilities, and innovation across three decades. This implies diffusion-oriented policy should build firms’ absorptive capacity.
papers.reason: Provides a methodological and thematic overview of the technological transformation literature with only indirect relevance to macro growth.

papers.title: Identification of Macroeconomic Clusters in the European Union Before and After 2020
papers.abstract: Macroeconomic indicators of European Union member states are essential for analyzing patterns of comparative economic development, identifying structural differences, and designing policies aimed at reducing regional disparities. This study applies cluster and discriminant analysis to group countries according to selected indicators and to determine the variables that contribute most to differentiating more developed and less developed member states. Principal component analysis (PCA) was employed to reduce data dimensionality and identify latent structures among countries, while factor analysis provides exploratory evidence consistent with the role of selected variables in shaping economic profiles. The results reveal the existence of a stable core of countries with high GDP and favourable fiscal positions, whereas Southern and Eastern European countries exhibit greater internal differences, particularly in inflation rates, unemployment, and public debt. Cluster and factor patterns indicate the consistency of country typologies across both periods, and PCA highlights more complex latent structures and potential convergence processes among certain country groups. These findings provide a solid foundation for understanding the dynamics of macroeconomic processes and planning future comparative analyses and policies, including guidance for targeted economic interventions and strategies to reduce regional inequalities, for both academic research and policy formulation. Measured as an annual rate rather than a price-level index, inflation is shown to diverge markedly after 2020, whereas real convergence in GDP per capita and unemployment continues; endogenous structural-break tests support a break around 2020, and internal validation indices support a stable three-cluster typology.
papers.reason: The study uses cluster and principal component analysis to map structural differences and convergence among EU member states, offering background context for sovereign debt and European policy analysis.

papers.title: Government debt dynamics in the EU after the pandemic: the role of the snowball effect
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent economic recovery had a strong impact on government debt dynamics in the EU. This paper focuses on fiscal developments in the period 2021-2023, when the economic crisis triggered by the pandemic had already passed. In particular, it aims to determine whether the rapid reduction in government debt ratios in that period was driven by member states’ primary surpluses or a favourable snowball effect – the positive difference between member states’ nominal growth rates and the average interest rates on their debt. The analysis clearly reveals that the snowball effect was the key factor behind the favourable trend in debt ratios. The paper also discusses the challenges and adverse shocks that the EU faced in the post-pandemic period, which put pressure on national budgets and thus contributed to the persistence of primary deficits in that period.
papers.reason: The paper analyses post-pandemic EU fiscal developments and debt reduction drivers, providing useful context for sovereign debt and rates strategists.

papers.title: Driving policy for low-carbon health care by data: asthma inhaler prescriptions in Norway, 2004-2025
papers.abstract: Abstract Issue Asthma inhalers contribute to health sector greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through Apaflurane and Norflurane in pressurized metered dose inhalers (pMDIs). Norwegian policy therefore recommends prescribing dry powder inhalers with lower emissions (DPIs) when this is assumed to give the same clinical benefit. Description of the problem To assess prescribing patterns and enable targeted policy action, we obtained data on inhaler prescriptions from the Norwegian Prescription Database. The primary aim was to estimate total emissions from pMDIS, to inform prescribers and authorities of pMDI inhalers’ climate footprint. A second aim was to explore a possible indicator on municipalities’ prescribing patterns, so that local quality work on inhaler use can support sustainable prescribing. We first categorised all 740 products for obstructive airways diseases (ATC code R03) by propulsion mechanism. Then we obtained national data on inhaler prescriptions 2004-2025. Results Estimated GHG emissions from pMDIs in recent years (when product availability was similar) were 27 945 (2022) to 31 215 (2025) tons of CO2. This amounts to 0.057%-0.074% of direct Norwegian CO2 emissions (scope 1) in this period. To assess variation in prescribing among patients where DPIs might be a viable clinical option, we defined a sustainable prescribing index as the number of pMDI inhalers prescribed divided by all inhalers prescribed, in municipalities with more than 100 users of inhalers per year. Nationally, the index was 15.1% in 2004 and 45.1% in 2025. On a municipal level, the index ranged from 4.2%-41.7% in 2004 and from 22.5%-62.4% in 2025. Lessons In this preliminary analysis of a national dataset, we confirm pMDIs as an appreciable and apparently a growing source of GHG emissions, with substantial variation in prescribing practice across municipalities. This suggests that national and local policy action to support sustainable prescribing has high potential for reducing emissions. Key messages • Pressurised Metered Dose Inhalers used in asthma treatment are an appreciable and apparently growing source of greenhouse gas emissions in Norway’s health sector. • Having access to a sustainable prescribing index (based on the proportion of pMDI prescribed) may support municipalities towards a sustainable prescribing practice.
papers.reason: Quantifies greenhouse gas emissions from asthma inhalers in Norway to inform local health policy, with negligible macro or market relevance.

papers.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
papers.abstract: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions. We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million. It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification. To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise. Hidden evaluation checks feasibility and compares objective quality against original expert solutions accepted by clients before benchmark construction. Deployment-Adjusted Quality (DAQ) averages expert-relative quality across instances, assigning zero to infeasible deliveries. Across 11 frontier LLMs using coding-agent harnesses, several exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality, but none matches its DAQ; the strongest primary Claude Code configuration achieves 88.39% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.87 against the expert reference of 1. Client information acquisition extends beyond clarification into solution development and validation, with some later stages showing higher confirmed issue-resolution proportions. Trajectory analysis identifies formulation and implementation failures, while task-equalized research-chain completion rates range from 24% to 45% across models on evaluable tasks. These findings motivate sustained information-gap resolution, faithful problem formulation, and evidence-linked self-improvement for reliable long-horizon agents.
papers.reason: Evaluates LLM performance on industrial operations research benchmarks, offering little direct relevance to macroeconomic or financial market analysis.

papers.title: Household demand for retail bonds and time deposits: The case of Poland - replication package
papers.abstract: This is the replication package for the paper Łesyk, M., Wesołowski, G., 2026. Household demand for retail bonds and time deposits: The case of Poland. This repository contains the data and R code which replicates all empirical results, figures, and tables included in the above-mentioned article. Abstract: We examine household demand for retail government bonds and time deposits in Poland, a small open economy where households can purchase government bonds directly. Our analysis extends a literature focused on the U.S., where indirect household Treasury debt holdings dominate. Using issue-level data, we construct a bond aggregate and estimate the elasticity of substitution between bonds and deposits. We find that these assets are imperfect substitutes, with an estimated elasticity somewhat above the U.S. benchmark. Interestingly, when longer-maturity bonds are excluded from the bond aggregate we cannot reject perfect substitution with time deposits. Next, we construct a broader asset aggregate of bonds and deposits and find that demand for it is negatively related to the opportunity-cost spread, consistent with theory and U.S. evidence. Our findings suggest effective monetary policy transmission to household assets and a need for active bond issuance policy in countries like Poland. Availability Status of the Data: All data are publicly available and sources are disclosed (see README file). All data series are included in the replication package.
papers.reason: Analyzes substitution between retail government bonds and time deposits in Poland, offering direct insights into monetary policy transmission and retail funding dynamics.

papers.title: Measuring Rental Feasibility: A Multidimensional Alternative to HRAI
papers.abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to present and empirically validate the Rental Feasibility Index (RFI), a multidimensional measure of the real capacity to rent a dwelling from the perspective of households. The index integrates four components: affordability, availability of rental offers, upfront costs, and financial stability. The study also provides a critical extension of the commonly used Housing Rental Affordability Index (HRAI), highlighting the need to incorporate additional dimensions of rental feasibility. The analysis uses monthly data for the Polish rental market from 2021 to 2026, enabling an assessment of the dynamics of the RFI, its components, and their interrelationships. The results show that the RFI effectively captures both short‑term shocks and long‑term trends. In 2022, the index recorded a sharp decline, driven mainly by a collapse in rental offer availability and a deterioration in household financial stability. In the following years, all components gradually recovered, with affordability and upfront costs exerting the strongest influence on the RFI. A comparison with the traditional HRAI revealed a moderate relationship, confirming that the two indicators capture different aspects of rental market conditions. Despite certain limitations, the RFI offers a useful tool for analysing the rental market and supporting housing policy.
papers.reason: Introduces and validates a multidimensional rental feasibility index using Polish housing market data, with clear implications for real estate and consumer financial stability.

papers.title: New evidence on consumer price rigidity in Poland
papers.abstract: Nominal rigidities play a central role in monetary policy transmission, shaping how inflation and real activity respond to various shocks. Using a large longitudinal dataset of granular price data for Poland covering 2000–2024, we contribute to the literature on price stickiness by documenting key features of price-setting behaviour in Poland. First, overall price stickiness in Poland is substantial, with the average (median) implied price duration of four (over six) months. Second, there is considerable heterogeneity and asymmetry present at the sectoral level. Third, the size of price changes is large, underscoring the importance of idiosyncratic shocks in price formation. Fourth, there is little evidence of downward nominal price rigidity outside the services sector, while there is strong evidence that price discounts play a significant role for price-setting. Finally, in recent years the frequency of price changes has increased broadly, indicating strengthened effectiveness of monetary policy in bringing inflation back to target.
papers.reason: Using granular pricing data in Poland, the paper documents price stickiness and changing frequency of price adjustments, informing monetary policy transmission and inflation dynamics in Europe.

papers.title: Hours or Heads? Demand Shocks and Labour Market Adjustments in Poland
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the role of demand shocks in driving labour market dynamics in Poland, an economy that transitioned from very high to low and stable unemployment despite repeated adverse shocks. Our contribution is threefold. First, we propose two complementary sign-restricted Bayesian VAR models that distinguish between labour-extensive and labour-intensive aggregate demand shocks, where the former operate primarily through changes in employment, while the latter mainly affect workers’ effort and hours per worker. Despite different specifications, both models yield highly consistent results. Second, we find that labour-extensive demand shocks are a key driver of unemployment, labour-intensive demand shocks primarily affect output, prices, and productivity, whereas both shocks are similarly important for hours per worker. Third, we document that the relative importance of these shocks changes over time, suggesting that the dominant margin of labour market adjustment may depend on economic conditions and the policy environment.
papers.reason: Identifies the role of demand shocks in driving Polish labor market adjustments and inflation dynamics, relevant for regional macroeconomic analysis.

papers.title: Replication package for "Demographic transition and the rise of wealth inequality"
papers.abstract: This replication package accompanies: Krzysztof Makarski, Joanna Tyrowicz, and Piotr Zoch. (forthcoming). "Demographic transition and the rise of wealth inequality". Economic Journal.

papers.title: Threshold Regression with a Nearly Integrated Threshold Variable
papers.abstract: This paper considers threshold regression with an integrated or local-to-unity threshold variable and a threshold fixed in levels. We study the least squares threshold estimator and establish its asymptotic theory under both fixed and diminishing threshold effects. Under a fixed effect, the threshold estimator has a compound Cox argmin limit, whereas under a diminishing effect, its limiting distribution is characterized by a two-sided Brownian argmax with a random scale. We also develop likelihood ratio inference, which is asymptotically pivotal under a diminishing effect and conservative under Gaussian errors for a fixed effect, and show that conventional $t$-ratios for the slope coefficients remain asymptotically standard normal. A sup-Wald test is proposed to detect threshold effects that may be too small for consistent threshold localization. We further extend the framework to allow for integrated slope regressors and for contemporaneous endogeneity of the threshold variable, showing that the leading endogenous contribution cancels over shrinking threshold windows. Monte Carlo simulations examine the finite-sample performance of the proposed methods. An illustration using public debt and economic growth highlights the relevance of allowing for a persistent threshold variable.
papers.reason: The paper develops asymptotic theory for threshold regression with persistent variables and illustrates it with public debt and growth data, holding clear methodological value for quantitative researchers.

papers.title: Technológiai szuverenitás és zöld ipar: a kínai iparpolitika új korszaka
papers.abstract: A tanulmány a kínai gazdaság zöld átállását a Made in China 2025 (MIC2025) program mentén elsősorban iparpolitikai és technológia szempontból vizsgálja. Ennek részeként bemutatja, hogy miként lépett túl Kína a „világ gyára” szerepkörön, milyen hosszú távú célrendszer szerint szerveződik a MIC2025, és hogyan épül be a zöld technológiai fejlesztés – a félvezetőktől a megújuló energián át az intelligens gyártásig –, valamint a zöld innováció a stratégiai ágazatok fejlesztési logikájába. Az elemzés arra a következtetésre jut, hogy a program vállalati szintű innovációs hatásai empirikusan kimutathatók, ugyanakkor erősen egyenlőtlenek régiók és tulajdonosi formák szerint, míg a környezeti célok számszerű teljesülése egyelőre vegyes képet mutat.
papers.reason: The study examines China's industrial policy and green technological development under the Made in China 2025 initiative, providing structural context for EM growth.

papers.title: A Perzsa-öböl menti légitársaságok üzletpolitikájának néhány kiemelt tartalmi eleme az utasok véleményének aspektusából
papers.abstract: The two decades preceding the COVID-19 pandemic constitute a well-defined and exceptionally successful time in the history of aviation for the airlines of the Persian Gulf region. Their dynamic development, efficient operational mechanisms, and the innovations they introduced in the field of services played a decisive role in shaping the landscape of global aviation. The exploration of the brand and marketing elements that form an important segment of their business policy has been documented in several of our previous publications. However, the opinions of the passengers have not yet been presented, even though we conducted an extensive investigation on this topic. In this study, we undertake to summarise the results of this broad dataset. Its relevance stems from the very need for feedback, which is a prominent element of the business philosophy of the companies examined, but this synthesis also complements our previous work and makes it more complex. In this empirical research, we measured and analysed the content of the service portfolio in relation to travellers’ reactions, the anomalies between brand identity and brand image, the perceived role of the central hubs placed at the focus of the airlines’ global expansion, and the cohesive strength of customer loyalty/commitment expected or desired from the target audience.
papers.reason: Focuses on passenger opinions and business policies of Persian Gulf airlines, with no relevance to financial markets or macroeconomic research.

papers.title: The Test of Confidence: An Interrupted Time Series Analysis of the Liquidity Effects of the VIBER ISO 20022 Migration
papers.abstract: This study examines the liquidity effects of the migration of the Hungarian Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system (VIBER) operated by the Central Bank of Hungary (MNB) to the ISO 20022 messaging standard. The objective is to determine whether the 27 October 2025 go-live resulted in a detectable structural break or a persistent change in the trend of VIBER’s aggregate closing balance. The empirical analysis is based on interrupted time series (ITS) segmented regression, complemented by robustness checks using ARIMA models. The initial regression results indicated a temporary decline in balances and a post-migration change in trend. However, after controlling for VAT payment periods, the temporary effect was no longer statistically significant. In the ARIMA models accounting for the autoregressive structure of the time series, neither the shock associated with the migration nor the post-migration change in trend proved robust. The findings suggest that a substantial proportion of the observed balance movements can be explained by the internal dynamics of the time series and by liquidity reallocations associated with tax payment periods. Interviews conducted with bank liquidity management specialist further confirmed that the migration did not require any extraordinary liquidity-management adjustments. Overall, the results indicate that the VIBER ISO 20022 migration was implemented without significant liquidity disruptions, which points to the successful preparation of project and to the high level of market confidence in the central bank.
papers.reason: Provides granular evidence on domestic payment system migration in Hungary, showing no systemic liquidity disruptions after controlling for tax calendars.

papers.title: Macroprudential Policy and Downside Risk: Regime-Dependent Effects of Capital Regulation
papers.abstract: This paper employs a Threshold Bayesian Vector Autoregression (TBVAR) to estimate the regime-dependent macroeconomic effects of capital regulation in Hungary. Using the Factor-based Index of Systemic Stress (FISS) as the threshold variable, the model identifies normal and stress regimes consistent with the occasionally binding constraints literature. The TBVAR offers a practical multivariate alternative to Growth-at-Risk for data-constrained economies. Generalised impulse responses reveal a pronounced asymmetry: releasing regulatory capital during stress raises GDP growth at the peak, with effects persisting for roughly twenty months, while the cost of accumulating capital in the normal regime is economically negligible. These findings are robust to alternative Cholesky orderings, sample periods, and credit variable definitions, providing direct empirical support for the countercyclical operation of the capital buffer.
papers.reason: Evaluates regime-dependent effects of bank capital regulation on GDP growth during stress and normal times, directly relevant for banking stability and credit.

papers.title: Temporal persistence thresholds for discontinuous higher-order contagion
papers.abstract: Abstract Higher-order contagion models show that group interactions can create tipping points: small outbreaks die out, while larger ones persist. In temporal systems, group interactions do not simply exist or not exist; they appear, disappear, and sometimes persist over time. This paper investigates when that persistence is strong enough to matter qualitatively. A minimal SIS contagion model with ordinary pairwise transmission and an additional triadic reinforcement mechanism is studied. The key assumption is that higher-order transmission requires a candidate triangle to be active in two consecutive observation windows. This gives a persistence-dependent reinforcement term derived from an explicit microscopic rule. Under a homogeneous mean-field closure, closed-form expressions are obtained for the bistability boundary, the critical persistence threshold, and the unstable seed-size threshold. The result is an analytical criterion showing when repeated small-group interactions are persistent enough to generate tipping-point epidemic behavior in the model. Finite-population simulations reproduce the persistence-controlled transition qualitatively, while explicit sparse-network simulations reveal a systematic reduction in realized triadic exposure compared to the homogeneous closure.
papers.reason: This is a theoretical and mathematical paper on contagion networks and SIS models without application to financial markets or macroeconomic data.

papers.title: Transparency and accountability as drivers of cultural change. A comparative analysis of central banks and national competent authorities
papers.abstract: Central banks and financial supervisory authorities make decisions that affect people, markets and the economy as a whole. Although legitimacy and public trust in public institutions generally depend on their ability to explain what they do, why they act and how they can be held to account through transparent and accountable governance, these considerations are especially important for central banks and financial supervisory authorities. Given their independence from day-to-day political direction and the limited direct political oversight to which they are subject, openness, effective communication and meaningful stakeholder participation play a critical role in maintaining their credibility and democratic legitimacy. Building on this premise, this paper examines the role of transparency and accountability in shaping institutional culture, strengthening legitimacy and fostering trust in this type of independent authority. While a substantial body of literature has examined transparency in specific policy areas, particularly monetary policy and financial stability, this paper adopts a broader governance perspective. It explores how national central banks and national competent authorities promote openness, communicate with stakeholders and the wider public and remain accountable in their day-to-day activities. In this context, transparency is understood not merely as the disclosure of information, but as a core governance function that underpins effective communication, meaningful public engagement and robust accountability arrangements. The analysis combines theory with comparative evidence from a structured questionnaire answered by 30 institutions in EU Member States and five institutions from non-EU jurisdictions. The questionnaire covered legal frameworks, internal arrangements, communication practices, access to information, participation mechanisms and accountability relationships.The findings show that transparency is increasingly more than a legal obligation to publish information. Most participating institutions go beyond minimum legal requirements by publishing additional material, using digital channels, adapting messages to different audiences, supporting financial literacy and creating opportunities for public engagement. At the same time, accountability is shown to operate through a multilayered set of relationships, including reporting duties, parliamentary and audit oversight, review and complaint mechanisms, public explanation and feedback channels that connect institutions both to formal oversight bodies and to society. The study also identifies areas where progress remains uneven, including the evaluation of transparency after publication, the measurement of communication effectiveness, and the transparency of processes supported by artificial intelligence. It concludes that transparency and accountability can drive institutional change when they are embedded in strategy, communication, internal governance, oversight and evaluation. The paper proposes a framework of good practices and a maturity index to help institutions move from compliance-driven transparency towards a more trust-based, evaluative and citizen-oriented approach to accountability, while preserving their independence.
papers.reason: The paper provides a comparative institutional governance analysis of central bank transparency and accountability, offering indirect context for central bank credibility rather than actionable market signals.

papers.title: 17-OH progesterone diagnostic cut-off for non-classic CAH in adult Bulgarian hyperandrogenic women
papers.abstract: Background: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) is an autosomal recessive disease, most commonly caused by 21-hydroxylase enzyme deficiency. The milder non-classic CAH form is characterized by adrenal androgen excess and might be a diagnostic challenge in the differential diagnosis of hyperandrogenic states. The „gold“ standard for CAH diagnosis is the synthetic ACTH (1-24) test; however, in some countries, e.g., Bulgaria, the test substance is not routinely available. Methods: The present study explores synthetic ACTH (1-24) test results in adult Bulgarian hyperandrogenic patients (n=93) to identify baseline morning 17-OH progesterone values associated with the lowest and highest risk of having non-classic CAH. Results: A morning 17-OH progesterone level of 10.68 nmol/l, measured by radioimmunoassay, has 100% sensitivity and 88% specificity for the diagnosis of non-classic CAH in a group of adult hyperandrogenic Bulgarian patients. A 17-OH progesterone cut-off value of 17.55 nmol/l showed 85% sensitivity and 100% specificity as a predictor of non-classic CAH in the same group. Conclusions: Hyperandrogenic Bulgarian patients with baseline morning 17-OH progesterone levels above 17.5 nmol/L may be referred directly for genetic CYP21A2 analysis, if the synthetic ACTH (1-24) test is unavailable, due to the high non-classic CAH risk. More administrative efforts are needed to ensure equal access to diagnostic tests and genetic investigations for all patients with CAH in Europe and worldwide.
papers.reason: This is a medical research paper on diagnostic cut-offs for congenital adrenal hyperplasia in patients, with no market relevance.

papers.title: Teaching Safety Skills for Emergency Situations to Autistic Individuals: A Rapid Literature Review
papers.abstract: Abstract Emergency situations are unexpected events that pose a threat of serious and immediate risk to safety. Difficulties in social communication and restricted behaviour mean that some autistic individuals may be vulnerable to harm during these events. However, skills can be taught to minimise this risk and increase the likelihood that autistic people can respond safely to such situations. This rapid review identified empirical studies teaching emergency related safety skills to autistic children and adults. Studies were assessed for quality against the What Works Clearinghouse standards. Forty studies were identified, with 143 autistic individuals (mean age 9.3 years, range 3–25 years) across 10 scenarios. A wide range of teaching methodologies were used, e.g., Behaviour Skills Training. Interventions that taught skills in the actual environment (in-situ) were most effective. Overall, the findings indicate positive outcomes in acquisition, generalisation and maintenance of skills. However, over half of the studies did not meet minimum quality standards, gaps remain in the range of scenarios addressed, and there is a notable scarcity of studies focused on skills acquisition for older autistic adults. There are opportunities to utilise technology-mediated environments such as Virtual Reality to teach skills in relation to events that are difficult to simulate.
papers.reason: This is a medical and social science review on teaching safety skills to autistic individuals with no relevance to financial markets.

papers.title: Sporadic inclusion body myositis: overreliance on histology may lead to misdiagnosis
papers.abstract: We describe a 57-year-old man who had initial isolated weakness in the deep finger flexors of his non-dominant hand, followed by quadriceps weakness and wasting a year later. Despite the distribution specific for sporadic inclusion body myositis (s-IBM) and early myogenic abnormalities found in deep finger flexors, the case was initially misdiagnosed as polymyositis based on the initial biopsy results, which revealed endomysial inflammation with partial invasion/compression of non-necrotic fiber, without rimmed vacuoles. As a result, the patient received unnecessary treatment, including immunosuppressants, which caused serious side effects. The second biopsy revealed rimmed vacuoles, and the diagnosis of s-IBM was confirmed. The role of clinical, pathological, and electrophysiological features for early diagnosis of s-IBM and differentiation from PM is discussed.

papers.title: U.S. Regional Business Cycles and the Natural Rate of Unemployment
papers.abstract: Estimates of the natural rate of unemployment are important in many macroeconomic models used by economists and policy advisors. This paper shows how such estimates might benefit from closer attention to regional developments. Regional business cycles do not move in lock-step, and greater dispersion among regions can affect estimates of the natural rate of unemployment. There is microeconomic evidence that employers are more reluctant to cut wages than they are to raise them. Accordingly, the relationship between wage inflation and vacancies is convex: An increase in vacancies raises wage inflation at an increasing rate. The authors' empirical results are consistent with this and indicate that if all else had remained constant, the reduction in the dispersion of regional unemployment rates between 1982 and 2000 would have meant a two-percentage-point drop in the natural rate of aggregate unemployment.
papers.reason: Demonstrates how regional US labor market dispersion affects macroeconomic estimates of the natural rate of unemployment.

papers.title: Analysis of the IMF’s Debt Sustainability Framework and Its Critique
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper evaluates the IMF’s debt sustainability analyses (DSAs), delving into their methodologies and implications and highlighting their problems. Since 2002, the DSAs have been the cornerstone of the IMF programs, providing the primary analytical tool to justify and determine the paths and targets specified. Although the DSAs have evolved significantly over time, they have severe foundational problems. They heavily rely on strong assumptions and staff judgments, and thereby, they are primarily non-transparent. Secondly, there are significant issues regarding the conduct of DSAs. They have grown excessively complex, hindering consensus on components without necessarily improving assessment quality. Thirdly, the IMF makes very high-stakes decisions with low precision, relying on persistent over-optimism in growth forecasting and paving the way for tighter fiscal policies. Fourthly, the debt dynamics equation of DSAs is inconsistent with stock flow dynamics because it focuses heavily on the primary balance as the main driver. Fifthly, the IMF’s framework does not pay enough attention to the underlying reasons for accumulating external debt in developing nations. It often treats external borrowing as a substitute for domestic debt without accounting for the asymmetric international financial architecture.
papers.reason: The paper evaluates IMF debt sustainability frameworks and their application to developing nations, offering relevant perspectives for emerging market sovereign debt analysis.

papers.title: Workforce Aging and Firm Productivity: Evidence from Türkiye
papers.abstract: Abstract Does workforce aging lower firm productivity? We study this question for a large emerging economy using matched employer–employee records from Türkiye linked to firm balance sheets over 2013–2023, roughly 1.75 million firm–year observations. Identifying the relationship from within-firm variation, we find that a higher share of older workers is associated with modestly lower productivity: a one-unit increase in the share of workers aged 50 and above lowers value added per worker by about 8.3 %. Much of the larger raw correlation reflects sorting of younger workforces into more productive firms, but a precise negative effect survives selection. The average conceals pronounced heterogeneity: the penalty is about 11 % in manufacturing and routine-intensive services, roughly half as large in construction and trade, and statistically absent in agriculture. Interacting the firm’s age composition with task scores confirms the mechanism: the penalty is attenuated where non-routine interpersonal content is high and amplified where routine and analytical content are high. What matters is less the age of a workforce than the work it performs. This is among the first firm-level evidence on aging and productivity for a large emerging economy.
papers.reason: The study offers granular firm-level evidence on workforce aging and productivity in a major emerging market, informing structural growth and labor market dynamics.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Health Expenditures and Growth Under Regimes Determined by Changes in Energy Taxes: A Panel Threshold Regression Approach
papers.abstract: This study aims to empirically examine whether the relationship between changes in health expenditures and economic growth exhibits a non-linear structure depending on changes in the ratio of energy tax revenues to GDP. In this context, annual data for the 2014–2021 period across 27 European countries are analyzed using a panel threshold regression method capable of uncovering structural differences across regimes. The empirical findings indicate that the rate of change in the energy tax revenue-to-GDP ratio serves as a statistically significant threshold variable in the model, exhibiting multi-threshold characteristics. Accordingly, the macroeconomic impacts of shifts in health expenditures on economic growth vary across regimes depending on the identified threshold values. In the first regime, characterized by a substantial decline in the energy tax revenue-to-GDP ratio, the effect of changes in health expenditures on growth is not statistically significant. Conversely, in the second regime, where the reduction in the energy tax revenue-to-GDP ratio is moderate, the negative impact of shifts in health expenditures on growth reaches its peak intensity. In the third regime, which encompasses minor declines, zero change, or positive changes in the energy tax revenue-to-GDP ratio, the negative effect persists, albeit with a diminished coefficient magnitude. In conclusion, the study demonstrates that the macroeconomic reflections of the interaction between energy tax revenue dynamics and health expenditures are non-linear and display regime-dependent asymmetric patterns.
papers.reason: The paper examines the non-linear relationship between health expenditures and growth conditional on energy taxes across European countries, providing niche fiscal insights.

papers.title: Türkiye’de Tarımsal Destekler ve Üretim İlişkisi
papers.abstract: Küresel iklim değişikliği, jeopolitik belirsizlikler ve tarımsal girdi maliyetlerindeki artış, gıda arz güvenliğini ve tarımsal üretimin sürdürülebilirliğini ciddi biçimde tehdit etmektedir. Tarımsal destek politikaları hem üretim istikrarının sağlanması hem de kırsal gelirlerin korunması açısından kritik bir politika aracı olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Bu çalışma, Türkiye’de uygulanan tarımsal desteklerin bitkisel ve hayvansal üretim üzerindeki etkilerini ampirik olarak incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır. Analizde, Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığı Çiftçi Kayıt Sistemi’ne (ÇKS) kayıtlı işletmelere ait 2019–2023 dönemini kapsayan il ve ilçe düzeyinde panel veriler kullanılmıştır. Bitkisel üretimde mazot ve gübre desteği ile fark ödemeleri; hayvancılıkta ise buzağı ve çiğ süt destekleri temel politika değişkenleri olarak ele alınmıştır. Üretim ve verimlilik üzerindeki etkiler, ürün, bölge ve yıl sabit etkilerini içeren çoklu regresyon modelleri aracılığıyla tahmin edilmiştir. Modellerde ayrıca iklim koşulları ve yapısal özellikler kontrol edilmiştir. Elde edilen bulgular, bitkisel üretimde mazot ve gübre desteği ile fark ödemelerinin üretim miktarı ve verimlilik üzerinde istatistiksel olarak anlamlı ve pozitif etkilere sahip olduğunu göstermektedir. Bununla birlikte, desteklerin üretim hacmi üzerindeki etkisinin verimlilik artışına kıyasla daha güçlü olduğu tespit edilmiştir. Hayvancılık desteklerinde ise buzağı ve çiğ süt desteklerinin hayvan varlığını artırıcı yönde etkili olduğu, ancak verimlilik üzerindeki etkilerin daha sınırlı kaldığı görülmektedir. Ayrıca çalışma, tarımsal desteklerin üretim kapasitesini artırmada etkili olduğunu ortaya koymakla birlikte, uzun vadede verimlilik odaklı, hedefli ve yapısal dönüşümü destekleyen politika tasarımlarının önemine işaret etmektedir.
papers.reason: Empirical analysis of agricultural support policies in Turkey provides sector-specific micro-level insights with limited direct relevance to broader macroeconomic or financial market trends.

papers.title: Blended Finance and Female Entrepreneurship
papers.abstract: Abstract We study the real and allocative consequences of relaxing gender-specific credit constraints by analyzing a blended finance program designed to expand bank lending to female entrepreneurs in Turkey. Merging credit registry, tax, and matched employer-employee data, we find participating banks raised their credit share to women by over 18%, spanning repeat, poached, and first-time borrowers. Beneficiary firms invest more, grow employment, sales, and profits, diversify their networks, and exit less. Treated banks also expand lending to male entrepreneurs, though the increase is smaller and disproportionately directed toward higher-productivity firms, suggesting reallocation rather than crowding out. District-level effects are absent, reecting the program’s modest scale.
papers.reason: Examines the effects of a blended finance program on credit registry data in Turkey, offering useful insights on targeted lending policies and firm performance in emerging markets.

papers.title: International Financial Centers, Foreign Direct Investment, and Economic Volatility
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Comparing economies with and without international financial centers (IFCs) over 1970–2023, with IFC status determined from the 121 centers ranked by the Global Financial Centres Index, we find that IFCs are not significantly associated with FDI inflows but are strongly associated with higher FDI outflows—1.2%–2.5% of GDP for non‐offshore IFCs and 11%–16% for offshore IFCs. Observed across both regional and global centers, this asymmetry suggests that IFCs are associated with capital sent abroad by domestic firms rather than capital brought in by foreign investors. In parallel, we find no robust evidence of a significant association between IFC presence—whether offshore or not—and economic volatility.
papers.reason: Analyzes the empirical link between international financial centers, foreign direct investment outflows, and economic volatility across a global panel.

papers.title: Propagation of Immigration Shocks through Firm-to-Firm Trade Networks,
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the extent to which an immigration shock to a region propagates through supply chains. Using the unexpected arrival of Syrian refugees, who are densely concentrated in border regions of Turkey, we estimate how firms across the country are affected in terms of sales, employment, and wages. We also examine the impact of the shock on interprovincial trade, focusing on trade volume and network formation. The results reveal positive spillover effects of immigration for firms with pre-existing links to Syrian refugee-hosting regions through upstream and downstream supply chain connections. Furthermore, we find evidence that the shock expands inter-provincial trade and contributes to the formation of new firm-to-firm linkages between provinces. Finally, we show that traditional spatial approaches that compare regions with differing migration rates may conflate cross-province propagation with the direct effect of migrants; in our setting, this conflation overstates direct effects on sales and employment at both the firm and regional levels of aggregation and masks a negative direct wage effect at the firm level.
papers.reason: Investigates how regional labor supply shocks propagate through firm-to-firm trade networks and impact inter-provincial trade in Turkey, offering useful insights for regional economic resilience and supply chain dynamics.

papers.title: Understanding labor market mismatches in Türkiye: evidence from the PIAAC survey
papers.abstract: Rapid expansion in educational attainment does not necessarily improve labor market outcomes when education systems fail to keep pace with labor demand. This paper examines education, skill, and field-of-study mismatch and their effects on wages and job satisfaction in a middle-income economy undergoing rapid educational expansion, using nationally representative PIAAC data for Türkiye. We employ both subjective and objective measures to identify mismatches and assess their relationship with wage outcomes and job satisfaction among full-time wage earners. The results show that labor market mismatch is widespread and multidimensional. Overall, 29% of full-time workers are educationally mismatched, while 41% experience skill mismatch. Among tertiary-educated workers, 34% are employed outside their field of study, with substantial overlap across different types of mismatch. Wage regressions reveal sizeable penalties associated with overeducation and overskilling, while required education yields the highest returns. Once educational mismatch is controlled for, field-of-study mismatch is no longer associated with additional wage penalties. In contrast, job satisfaction is positively associated with undereducation and underskilling. By jointly analyzing multiple mismatch dimensions and controlling for cognitive skills, the study contributes new evidence on labor market mismatch in developing and middle-income economies.
papers.reason: Analyzes education and skill mismatches and their wage penalties in Turkey, providing micro-level labor market analysis with limited direct application to near-term macroeconomic forecasting.

papers.title: Kripto Döngüsü ve ABD Para Politikası: Faktör Temelli VAR ve EKK Analizi
papers.abstract: This study examines the effects of U.S. monetary policy and global financial conditions on cryptocurrency prices over the period from April 2020 to May 2026. The common price dynamics of nine cryptocurrencies are summarized into a single latent cryptocurrency factor using Principal Component Analysis. The first principal component explains 74% of the total variance, confirming the existence of a dominant systemic factor underlying cryptocurrency markets. Short run dynamics are estimated through a VAR framework, while long run relationships are estimated using OLS with Newey–West HAC standard errors. Model robustness is verified through the AR characteristic polynomial and Bai–Perron multiple structural break tests. Impulse response analysis indicates that positive shocks to SOFR and the U.S. 2-year Treasury yield generate persistent negative responses in the cryptocurrency factor, whereas responses to its own innovations remain negative until approximately the thirtieth period, reflecting mean reversion dynamics. Forecast error variance decomposition attributes 98.89% of the factor’s variance to endogenous shocks, while commodity variables exert a greater exogenous influence than monetary policy variables. OLS estimates further reveal that gold and Brent oil significantly affect cryptocurrency valuations, whereas monetary policy variables exhibit delayed and shock driven effects. Overall, cryptocurrency prices exhibit a multi layered pricing structure shaped by endogenous momentum in the short run, monetary policy shocks in the medium run, and global commodity cycles together with structural growth trends in the long run.
papers.reason: Investigates the impact of U.S. monetary policy, commodity prices, and global financial conditions on cryptocurrency valuations.

papers.title: Labour Market Implications of Generative AI in an Emerging Economy: The Case of Türkiye
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly viewed as a general-purpose technology with far-reaching labour-market implications. While existing evidence is largely drawn from advanced economies, much less is known about the impact of generative AI on employment in emerging economies. This article examines the labour-market impact of generative AI in Türkiye using individual-level administrative records from the Social Security Institution combined with occupation-level exposure measures from the International Labour Organisation. We find that the share of AI-exposed employment within the top 20% of the exposure distribution (fifth quintile) amounts to 17% of total employment. About 2.3 million registered jobs in Türkiye are highly exposed to generative AI. Employment effects are strongly age-asymmetric: since 2023, job growth has weakened mainly for early-career workers in highly exposed occupations, while no comparable losses are observed for workers over thirty. These patterns survive controls for sectoral reallocation, suggesting that generative AI operates primarily through hiring margins, displacing inexperienced workers while complementing experienced ones.
papers.reason: Using administrative data from Türkiye, this paper evaluates the employment impact of generative AI on emerging market labour dynamics, providing useful inputs for structural growth and macroeconomic assessments.

papers.title: TCMB para politikası iletişimindeki geçişlerin doğal dil işleme ve yapay zekâ temelinde analizi
papers.abstract: Bu çalışmada, Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB) tarafından 2006-2025 yılları arasında yayınlanan para politikası basın duyuruları ile Para Politikası Kurulu (PPK) toplantı özetleri, bankanın iletişim stratejisindeki dönemsel geçişleri ve bu geçişlerin arkasındaki dinamikleri analiz etmek amacıyla incelenmiştir. Çalışma kapsamında elde edilen İngilizce metin setleri üzerinde dört temel doğal dil işleme yöntemi uygulanmıştır: (1) TF-IDF (biçimsel) ve SBERT (anlamsal) vektörleştirmesi kullanılarak kosinüs benzerliği analizi; (2) “facebook/bart-large-mnli” modeli ile Sıfır-Öğrenme Tasnifi (Zero-Shot Classification) duygu analizi; (3) Word2Vec (Skip-gram) yöntemiyle anlamsal kayma analizi; (4) Loughran McDonald (LM) sözlüğü kullanılarak belirsizlik ve kesinlik (kısıtlayıcılık) analizi. Analiz bulguları, basın duyurularının genel olarak yüksek bir tutarlılık sergilediğini, ancak toplantı özetlerinin özellikle dışsal şok dönemlerinde duyurulardan farklılaşarak daha dalgalı bir yapı izlediğini ortaya koymuştur. Duygu analizi sonuçları, politika metinlerinin tonunun faiz kararları öncesinde güçlü bir öncü gösterge olduğunu kanıtlarken; anlamsal kayma analizi, “istikrar” kavramının zaman içinde finansal istikrar vurgusundan fiyat istikrarı hedefine net bir şekilde evrildiğini göstermiştir. Ayrıca son dönem iletişiminde belirsizliğin azalmasıyla birlikte, veri odaklı ve esnek bir dil yapısının benimsendiği tespit edilmiştir. Bu çalışma, TCMB’nin piyasa beklentilerini yönlendirebilmek amacıyla iletişim stratejisini dönemsel şartlara uygun olarak dinamik biçimde değiştirdiğini ve para politikası metinlerinin analizinde yapay zekâ tekniklerinin kullanılmasının, karar dinamiklerini anlamlandırmada kritik rol oynadığını göstermesi bakımından literatüre katkı sunmaktadır.

papers.title: Local Currency Borrowing Constraints and Firm Behavior: Evidence from an Emerging Market
papers.abstract: We analyze the financial and real effects of a 2022 Turkish regulation that restricts new local currency lending to firms whose asset dollarization exceeds specified thresholds. Using novel administrative data from January 2021–December 2023 and a difference-in-differences approach combined with propensity score matching, we find a medium-term decline in local currency borrowing among affected firms with a stronger impact for credit-constrained firms. We also document spillover effects, as firms substitute local currency loans with foreign currency loans, Turkish lira trade credit, and internal foreign currency liquidity. Extended analysis indicates that employment growth and net exports of affected firms declined, while operational volatility increased.
papers.reason: The paper analyzes how credit restrictions on dollarized firms alter corporate borrowing, credit substitution, and operational performance using administrative data.

papers.title: Corporate dollar debt and balance sheet effects: identification using Trump tweets
papers.abstract: This paper revisits foreign exchange spillover effects via the balance sheet channel, exploiting exogenous shocks triggered by the US president Trump’s 2018 tweets of threatening imminent sanctions on Turkish exports. These tweets were politically driven and produced a large and unanticipated exchange rate shock within the Turkish economy, consequently providing a quasi-natural experiment to investigate the balance sheet channel of dollar-denominated corporate debt. Using quarterly data for 2013–2023 for firms listed on Borsa Istanbul, our difference-in-difference estimations around the window of Trump tweets show that firms with high net FX debt experienced a major decline in investment rates following the depreciation, whereas the control group remained largely unaffected. The identified impact is approximately twice the size of estimates obtained through standard panel data methods. Overall, this study contributes to the literature by providing a clear and rigorous identification strategy for FX spillover effects through the balance sheet channel.
papers.reason: Uses identified exchange rate shocks to quantify corporate debt balance sheet vulnerabilities and investment effects in an emerging market.

papers.title: The Role of Inflation Targeting in Placement of Household Savings in Nominal Contracts
papers.abstract: One distinctive feature of Russian households is that they hold a large proportion of their financial assets in nominal ruble contracts (or assets), that is, contracts whose nominal payment is fixed in rubles: bank deposits and bonds as well as cash. The purchasing power of savings held in such assets is subject to inflation risk. The author arrives at several key conclusions and policy recommendations aimed at maintaining the purchasing power of household savings. First, a nominal interest rate of 8.5% may be regarded as the minimum long-term threshold that provides sufficient incentives for long-term saving given large and historically frequent asymmetric (upward biased) inflationary shocks. Second, inflation targeting constitutes an important part of the incentive for keeping savings in nominal contracts. The introduction of inflation targeting in Russia in 2015 made it possible to systematically counteract the long-standing decline in the purchasing power of accumulated savings. Third, insofar as long-term macroeconomic stability depends on preserving the purchasing power of savings, the proposed inflation targeting regime entails that the policy rate should be increased in response to one-off inflationary shocks whether or not inflation expectations are well anchored. An inflation targeting approach which allows monetary policy to accommodate temporary price-level changes may cause permanent (cumulative) erosion of the purchasing power of savings. The paper concludes that the key factor that would support household savings is not inflation targeting per se, but rather the preservation of the inflation targeting approach that has been established in Russia over the past decade.
papers.reason: Examines the role of inflation targeting and interest rate thresholds in maintaining household savings in nominal contracts within Russia.

papers.title: SPATIAL DIFFERENTIATION OF FINANCIAL BEHAVIOR IN RUSSIA: IDENTIFYING NORTHERN REGIONS THROUGH CLUSTER ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: This article examines the financial behavior of the population in Russia’s northern regions. It is assumed that household consumption and savings behavior in these regions systematically differs from national averages due to unique climatic conditions. Therefore, an attempt is made to scientifically substantiate the classification of Russia's northern regions into a separate cluster based on the financial patterns of their residents. By northern regions, we mean the constituent entities of Russia whose territories have been legally designated (fully or partially) as the Far North. Using a variety of clustering methods, Russian regions were divided into five groups. It is worth noting that the northern regions consistently formed separate groups regardless of the method used, thus confirming our initial hypothesis about their uniqueness. Meanwhile, major economic centers (Moscow, St. Petersburg, and the Moscow Region) also fell into these groups. However, we believe that the high incomes and high savings per capita in the North are due to other factors. Furthermore, several border regions (for example, the Arkhangelsk Region) were identified as lagging behind most northern territories in terms of income levels. A hypothesis was also formulated regarding the different responses of the populations of the Far North regions to monetary policy, but this requires further verification. Overall, this article contributes to the body of literature on the economies of Russia’s northern territories with a focus on household finances, an area that remains relatively understudied.

papers.title: Elasticity of labour substitution for CGE, DSGE models given the Russian labour market rigidity
papers.abstract: The post-pandemic inflation rise globally and in individual countries particularly highlighted the importance of revisiting the issue of labour market rigidity. Conventionally, unemployment rate, mean wages’ pattern, ratio of number of job offers to the number of job seekers form a typical list of indicators to monitor labour market rigidity. At the same time, general equilibrium macroeconomic modelling encompasses the possibility of labour substitution in-between industries at least. However, such substitution is often limited to a single value. Moreover, regional or job-specific substitution effects are mostly omitted due to the complexity of extracting and modelling respective parameters. The typical solution to such model simplification was to consider a set of expert-based substitution parameter values. Here we rediscover the datasource on job postings which yields us a unique opportunity to deeply consider the interrelationships of labour across different industries, including the cross-substitution effects. Moreover, we provide calibration for the elasticity of substitution subject to geographical, industrial and skills’ differences. Our principal claim is that it is worth considering as the common constant elasticity of substitution (CES) parameter of labour substitution elasticity in-between professions in Russia.
papers.reason: Estimates elasticities of labour substitution across industries and regions in Russia using job posting data, supporting structural macro modelling for the country.

papers.title: On Digital Currency as Property for the Purposes of Inclusion in the Debtor’s Bankruptcy Estate in Insolvency Cases
papers.abstract: This article notes the differences between digital currency and things and property rights, highlighting legislator’s and courts’ approaches to defining digital currency as property under Article 128 of the Civil Code of the Russian Federation. It notes a tendency of the courts to consider digital currency as other property not only for the purposes of protecting the public interests and the interests of non-participants of the digital currency circulation, particularly when it is included in a debtor’s bankruptcy estate under Article 131 of the Russian Insolvency Law, but also to protect the interests of the digital currency owner or participants of its circulation.

papers.title: Productivity trends of Russian firms in 2018—2024
papers.abstract: This paper examines total factor productivity (TFP) dynamics among Russian enterprises from 2018 to 2024, using translogarithmic production function estimates for 290 industries. To address endogeneity and functional dependence issues, we employ the Ackerberg—Caves—Frazer methodology with a control function approach. Our findings reveal distinct sectoral patterns. In mining, both simple average and value-added-weighted TFP rose during 2020—2021, then declined in 2022. Manufacturing exhibited steady TFP growth from 2018 to 2022, with a sharp acceleration in 2023, followed by divergent trajectories: value-addedweighted TFP continued to increase, while simple average TFP fell in 2024. In trade, simple average TFP dropped markedly in 2021—2022 and had not recovered to baseline levels by 2024. The services sector, hardest hit by the COVID-19 pandemic, displayed a volatile growth path, with contractions in 2020 and 2022. Across all sectors, cumulative growth in value-added-weighted TFP consistently outpaced that of simple average TFP, pointing to significant within-sector firm heterogeneity and suggesting that larger enterprises are more resilient to shocks.
papers.reason: The study provides granular total factor productivity dynamics across Russian industries from 2018 to 2024, offering useful structural context on enterprise resilience under sanctions and shocks.

papers.title: The transmission of shocks across sectors and the dynamics of sectoral prices
papers.abstract: This paper studies the dynamics of U.S. sectoral producer prices in a large Bayesian Vector Auto Regression (BVAR) model where the Input-Output (IO) matrix is used to structure their long-run relationships. The model provides evidence of a sectoral spillover channel in driving headline inflation without imposing such a mechanism in the model’s structure. Forecasts of headline inflation have accuracy comparable to the Survey of Professional Forecasters’ and greater than those generated by a standard BVAR with the Minnesota prior, confirming that the IO matrix long-run prior conveys relevant information about the data. The study of an oil price shock shows that adding the production network prior alters the transmission of the shock, amplifying headline inflation. Across sectors, the peak price response to the oil shock increases with oil intensity. A narrowly sector-specific disturbance, such as a cereal price shock, has non-negligible aggregate effects once the production network is accounted for. Sectoral asymmetries are crucial for evaluating the macroeconomic consequences of macroeconomic shocks such as an energy price shock and a monetary policy shock, as industries with slower price adjustments amplify inflation persistence, even after the shock dissipates.
papers.reason: Demonstrates how input-output production networks amplify energy shocks and persistence in U.S. headline inflation using a large BVAR model.

papers.title: Commercial real estate debt financing in Europe: evidence from a network analysis
papers.abstract: The commercial real estate (CRE) sector is a source of financial stability risk, yet its financing structures remain poorly understood because of complex corporate groupstructuresanddatalimitations. Thispaperinvestigatesthefinancingnetworks of the 100 largest CRE groups in the euro area, constructing two distinct networks: one for loan financing and one for bond issuance. The loan network exhibits strong regional clustering, a pronounced home bias and a core-periphery structure. Regionaldifferencesinloanfinancingpatternsgiverisetogeographicallyconcentrated communities of CRE entities with similar characteristics. The backbone of the loan market shows limited overlap among banks, both in the set of CRE borrowers they serve and in the size and composition of their loan portfolios, pointing to segmented lending relationships. By contrast, the bond network displays greater interconnectedness, is largely free of home bias and allows access to a diversified investor base. Financial stability implications are assessed through the structural properties of the networks and the identification of systemic nodes. In the loan network,regionalclusteringmayamplifycross-bordercontagion,whilehighlycentral CRE groups in both networks could generate spillovers in distress, shaping credit allocation and systemic risk in the euro area.
papers.reason: Maps euro area commercial real estate financing networks, identifying structural vulnerabilities, regional clustering, and systemic risk transmission channels.

papers.title: Geopolitical Distance and Targeted Trade: Evidence from Product-Level Export Controls
papers.abstract: Trade policy in advanced economies is closely intertwined with concerns about technology and geopolitical rivalry.Using product-level data on export-related trade interventions, we characterize how contemporary export-side interventions are allocated across products, destinations, and bilateral trade relationships.We show that export controls are broad in regulatory scope but economically concentrated on high-value trade flows.Export controls disproportionately target high-technology products and economically important trade relationships, while geopolitical distance shapes their allocation in a nonlinear manner, with the strongest associations for high-technology trade between geopolitical rivals.Finally, a decomposition of targeting patterns shows that modern export controls are organized primarily around products rather than destinations, consistent with a technology-centered regulatory framework.
papers.reason: Examines product-level export controls in advanced economies, offering clear implications for global trade flows, supply chains, and cross-border corporate risk.

papers.title: Treasury Issuance and Dealer Balance Sheets
papers.abstract: Primary dealers play an important role as intermediaries in Treasury securities and repo markets, and demand for their intermediation rises on issuance dates. Recent increases in Treasury issuance have raised questions about dealers' capacity to meet this increased demand.
papers.reason: The paper examines dealer balance sheet capacity and intermediation demand on Treasury auction dates, directly informing rates trading and market liquidity dynamics.

papers.title: Automation and Inequality: How Robots Shift Income Between Workers and Owners
papers.abstract: We estimate the direct effects of robot adoption on the within-firm distribution of income between non-owner workers and individual owners in Canadian private corporations. We link firm-level data on industrial robot imports to matched owner-worker-firm data that identify owners of private corporations, their employment income, and firms’ dividend payments to owners and retained earnings. Robot adoption is associated with sizable increases in firm revenues, value added, and non-owner employment and payroll. Unlike several studies of robot adoption in other settings, we find little evidence that adoption reduces adopters’ conventionally measured labor share of value added; if anything, the non-owner labor share increases slightly, while the total owner income share does not rise. Owners nevertheless benefit from adoption, but primarily through increases in employment income. These results underscore the importance of distinguishing owner employment income from ordinary worker payroll for measuring how firm-level technology shocks affect workers, owners, and the distribution of income within firms.
papers.reason: Analyzes micro-level data on robot adoption in Canada, showing nuanced effects on firm revenues, payroll, and owner income distribution.

papers.title: Labor Markets, Financial Crises, and Inflation: Jobless and Wageless Recoveries*
papers.abstract: We document the macroeconomic patterns that characterize labor market recovery from financial crises. Using a sample of postwar recession episodes from around the world, we show that financial crises are typically followed by jobless recoveries, with a sluggish recovery in employment relative to output. A departure from this empirical regularity occurs in emerging-market crises with high inflation, which feature strong employment recoveries but persistent declines in real wages and result in “wageless recoveries.” Our findings highlight the central role of financial components in labor input costs and nominal wage rigidities in shaping labor market dynamics following economic crises.
papers.reason: Examines global post-crisis labor market dynamics, showing how financial crises produce jobless recoveries while high-inflation emerging markets experience wageless recoveries.

papers.title: Contributions to euro area inflation over arbitrary time periods
papers.abstract: In the euro area, inflation is measured by the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP). Contributions of specific products to the overall inflation rate are derived by what is known as the Ribe approach. While this approach can be applied to the monthly HICP indices, it cannot be used for the annual HICP averages published by statistical offices, nor can it be used to calculate contributions to inflation over multiple years. This paper develops a generalization of Ribe's approach that overcomes both limitations. For annually chain-linked Laspeyres-type indices and their quarterly and annual averages, the proposed method allows contributions to price changes to be derived over arbitrary time periods. The resulting contributions consistently sum to the overall price change. As such, the method provides a useful tool for long-term monetary policy analysis. An application to HICP data shows that services have been the main driver of inflation in the euro area since 2002.
papers.reason: Develops a generalized method for calculating HICP product contributions over arbitrary time horizons, aiding long-term euro area monetary policy analysis.

papers.title: Prewar US business cycles under uncertainty: reconstructing quarterly GDP before 1947
papers.abstract: Official quarterly US GDP estimates begin in 1947; earlier quarterly histories must be reconstructed using annual benchmarks and historical indicators. To investigate uncertainty in these reconstructions, this paper systematically compares specifications drawn from the literature for reconstructing quarterly GDP during 1919–1946. The comparison evaluates predictions on concealed postwar quarters and separates variation across specifications from coefficient uncertainty within a model.
papers.reason: The paper reconstructs pre-1947 US quarterly GDP data, offering methodological insights with limited direct relevance to current market pricing.

papers.title: Heterogeneity in Service Fee Sensitivity: Evidence from ATM Surcharges
papers.abstract: Service fees continue to proliferate in a wide range of markets, from retail to payments, generating questions about their impact on consumer choice, competition, and fairness. This paper explores how sensitivity to such fees varies across consumers, use cases, and competitive settings, and whether it is affected by consumer learning. I am able to conduct this in-depth empirical analysis thanks to a uniquely detailed, high-frequency panel data set on surcharged ATM cash withdrawals. Results show that average elasticity estimates mask substantial heterogeneity in consumer sensitivity to service fees. I explore ways in which market and behavioral mechanisms can help explain this heterogeneity. Finally, I investigate whether consumers strategically adjust their behavior in response to service fees.
papers.reason: It examines consumer sensitivity to ATM surcharge fees using micro-level panel data, offering indirect insights for retail banking and payment sectors.

papers.title: Measuring Consumption with Credit Card Data: Benchmarking and Beyond
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel monthly county-level consumption dataset constructed from spending data on over 350 million credit cards in the Federal Reserve’s Y-14M reports, covering over 3,000 U.S. counties since 2014. We first show that the data closely track traditional consumption measures, explaining 92 percent of the variation in monthly adjusted personal consumption expenditures (PCE) growth at the national level, capturing meaningful cross-sectional variation in annual adjusted PCE growth at the state level, and reproducing the impulse response of official consumption measures to identified monetary policy shocks. We then use the county-month panel to estimate heterogeneous consumption responses to monetary policy shocks across the county-level income distribution, an analysis infeasible with traditional consumption data. We find suggestive evidence that low-income counties exhibit larger spending declines than high-income counties, consistent with heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models. Finally, we provide practical guidance for researchers working with similar data, discussing coverage, sample composition, and the approximation of credit card spending from credit bureau data.
papers.reason: The paper introduces a high-frequency county-level consumption dataset using credit card data to evaluate heterogeneous spending responses to monetary policy shocks.

papers.title: Examining the Beliefs of Professional Forecasters
